title: GREEN BONDS AS A FINANCING TOOL FOR RENEWABLE ENERGY PROJECTS IN CENTRAL ASIA
summary: . The transition toward renewable energy has become a strategic priority for Central Asian countries seeking to strengthen energy security, diversify their economies, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. However, the implementation of large-scale renewable energy projects requires substantial long-term investment. Green bonds have emerged as an alternative financial instrument capable of mobilizing capital from institutional investors, development banks, and international financial markets. This article examines the role of green bonds in financing renewable energy projects in Central Asia, focusing on their potential, institutional requirements, and implementation challenges. Particular attention is paid to the development of green finance markets in Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan. The study argues that green bonds can support solar, wind, hydropower, and other sustainable energy projects by providing access to diversified sources of capital. Nevertheless, their effectiveness depends on transparent reporting, credible project selection, regulatory support, and the development of domestic capital markets.

title: Bridging Micro and Macro Sustainability: How Sustainable Finance Connects Corporate esg to Sustainable Development Goals
summary: ABSTRACT Sustainable finance (SF) has increasingly been conceptualized in the literature as a mechanism linking firm‐level ESG practices to broader sustainable development outcomes. However, the field remains theoretically fragmented, with limited integrated mapping of micro–SF–macro linkages. Using scientometric and bibliometric techniques, this study analyzes 1,024 Scopus‐indexed publications (2004–2025) through performance analysis, keyword co‐occurrence, text mining, and bibliographic coupling. Thirteen keyword clusters reveal the intellectual structure of the field, spanning green finance, ESG performance, governance, climate policy, and energy transition. Bibliographic coupling identifies six thematic clusters that suggest how sustainable finance is theorized to link firm‐level actions with macro‐level sustainability transformations. Despite rapid post–Paris Agreement growth, theoretical and methodological coherence remains limited. The study outlines future research directions, emphasizing disclosure harmonization, causal identification, innovation–policy alignment, and multi‐level approaches. Accordingly, the findings capture patterns in the literature rather than empirically verified causal relationships.

title: Corporate digital transformation improves carbon performance through green innovation and total factor productivity under varying financial conditions
summary: Against the background of low-carbon transition and increasing climate governance pressure, digital transformation (DT) has become an important way for firms to improve environmental performance and support green development. Using panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2012 to 2023, this study examines whether and how corporate DT improves carbon performance (CP) and how financial conditions shape this effect. The results show that DT has a positive and statistically significant effect on CP. This finding remains robust after a series of robustness checks and endogeneity tests. Mechanism analysis indicates that DT improves CP by promoting green innovation (GI) and enhancing total factor productivity (TFP). Moderation analysis further shows that the firm-level green credit ratio strengthens the positive effect of DT on CP, whereas financing constraints weaken it. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the effect is more evident among non-state-owned enterprises and large firms, while it remains broadly observed across different sectors and pollution intensities. By jointly examining transmission mechanisms and financial boundary conditions, this study provides firm-level evidence on how DT improves CP and offers implications for coordinating digital upgrading, green finance, and corporate low-carbon transition.

title: Urban ecological resilience in the digital era: the role of data factor marketization and spatial spillovers
summary: As data becomes an increasingly important production factor in the digital economy, its role in shaping environmental outcomes has attracted growing attention. This study examines how data factor marketization affects urban ecological resilience. Using a spatial difference-in-differences model and panel data from 282 Chinese cities between 2010 and 2022, we find that data factor marketization significantly enhances ecological resilience and generates positive spatial spillovers, although these effects are mainly concentrated within a relatively short geographic range. The effect operates through three main pathways: green innovation, efficient resource allocation, and industrial upgrading through digital transformation. The results also reveal substantial heterogeneity: eastern and western cities benefit more than central ones, and resource-based cities respond more strongly, likely due to their stronger demand for structural transformation. In addition, cities with stronger digital foundations derive greater ecological benefits from the reform, highlighting the conditioning role of digital development in shaping policy effectiveness. These findings advance understanding of how data factor allocation supports environmental adaptation and underscore the importance of digital infrastructure and institutional capacity. Policy efforts should prioritize data institutionalization, digital inclusion, and targeted support for digitally lagging and resource-dependent cities to better translate data reforms into ecological gains.

title: DETERMINANTS OF INVESTOR TRUST IN GREEN BONDS
summary: The importance of investor trust in ensuring that green bonds successfully mobilize funding for ecologically sustainable activities has increased due to the swift growth of green finance. However, the information and credibility mechanisms driving investor trust remain relatively understudied, especially in emerging markets. In the context of the Vietnamese market, this study aims to explore the relationship between investor trust in green bonds and Green Accounting Information Quality (GAIQ), Green Bond Disclosure Transparency (GBDT), External Review and Assurance (ERA), and Issuer ESG Reputation (IER). Using survey data from 369 ordinary investors and representatives of institutional investors, the study creates an integrated information-and-credibility paradigm based on information asymmetry and signaling viewpoints. The suggested relationships are evaluated using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM). The results show that investor trust is positively and considerably impacted by all four focus variables, with ERA having the greatest impact, followed by GAIQ, GBDT, and IER. The model accounts for 50.1% of the variance in investor trust, suggesting that investor trust is influenced by a variety of information and credibility mechanisms rather than only green labeling. By combining firm-level green accounting data, bond-specific disclosure, independent assurance, and issuer ESG reputation under a single investor-trust framework, the study adds to the literature on green finance and accounting. The results are especially pertinent to investors assessing the quality of green bonds and the risk of greenwashing; listed companies and financial managers looking to bolster the credibility of green bonds; accounting and assurance professionals in charge of sustainability information and verification; and policymakers and regulators creating disclosure, assurance, and investor-protection mechanisms for Vietnam's developing green bond market. Overall, the study emphasizes how crucial it is to combine reliable external and reputational signals with high-quality information in order to boost investor trust and promote the long-term growth of green financing.

title: Financial Innovation and Sustainable Business Practices
summary: The connection between financial innovations and sustainable business, offers a framework that combines FinTech usage, green finance tools and sustainability performance. In the course of the research using a mixed methods methodology (systematic literature review and cross-sectoral case analysis), the key mechanisms for sustainable business models enabled by financial technologies including blockchain, artificial intelligence and digital platforms have been determined. In particular, the framework outlines three paths through which financial innovations help to ensure sustainable business development: resource efficiency improvement through digital finance tools, ESG integration through innovative financial instruments and stakeholders' value creation through inclusive financial models. The analysis of recent initiatives of industry players shows that companies which use innovations to achieve sustainable development are characterized by better access to green finance, higher level of transparency of supply chains and more robust stakeholder relations.

title: Supply Chain Resilience through the Integration of Green Operations and Circular Economy
summary: Global supply chain disruptions, environmental pressures, and sustainability demands have encouraged manufacturing companies in Surabaya to increase operational resilience through the implementation of green operations and circular economy. This study aims to analyze the influence of the integration of green operations and circular economy practices on supply chain resilience in manufacturing companies in the city of Surabaya. The study used a quantitative approach with a survey of 150 respondents consisting of managers and operational, production, and supply chain managers and staff from Surabaya manufacturing companies. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Square (SEM-PLS). The results show that the integration of green operations and circular economy has a positive effect on improving supply chain resilience through efficiency, flexibility, and operational adaptability. This research makes a theoretical and practical contribution to the development of sustainable operational management strategies to deal with supply chain risks.

title: How sustainable finance initiatives and forums address environmental issues, including climate change, and the challenges they face
summary: Abstract An increasing number of transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums are focusing on shifting and mobilizing private finance. Consequently, it has become more difficult to grasp the big picture concerning their roles and effects, including how they overlap and synergize. This study examined how transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums contribute to scaling up private finance and investment and encourage private sector participation. It also explored the challenges that they face in achieving climate-related and other environmental goals. To assess the effectiveness and legitimacy of transnational governance, the institutional and actor-related dimensions and impacts of five major United Nations-related transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums were analyzed using an analytical framework that included the following elements: transparency, accountability, participation, environmental and other societal impacts, and academic and practical literature. This study showed that each of these initiatives and forums differed in its governing structure and approaches, as well as in its relationship with United Nations-related institutions and actors. Furthermore, overlapping institutions and actors were involved across initiatives and forums, with areas of collaboration between them. While each initiative successfully engaged diverse actors, common challenges emerged, including difficulty in evaluating and enhancing the effectiveness of transnational initiatives and forums, the need for effective links among transnational initiatives and other governance systems (e.g., effective institutional and actor interplay between these voluntary initiatives and compulsory interventions), and the need to include diverse actors. This study showed that more research is required to explore ways of evaluating and enhancing transnational governance of voluntary multistakeholder initiatives and to address the above challenges.

title: ESG FACTORS IN THE TRANSFORMATION OF UKRAINE’S FINANCIAL ARCHITECTURE: INVESTMENT DIMENSION AND SUSTAINABLE FINANCE
summary: This article examines the role of ESG factors in the transformation of Ukraine’s financial architecture in the context of sustainable development, focusing on investment processes and the development of sustainable finance. The theoretical foundations of the transformation of financial architecture under the influence of the concept of sustainable development and the integration of ESG criteria into investment activities are considered. The research analyzes the current trends and prospects for implementing sustainable financing instruments, in particular green bonds. Attention has also been paid to the development of sustainable banking and the incorporation of ESG factors into the operations of banking institutions. The key risks and barriers to sustainable investment in Ukraine have been identified. The challenges associated with adapting the Ukrainian securities market to international sustainable finance standards are analyzed, and the prospects for its integration into global financial flows are outlined. The article proposes a conceptual model of the impact of ESG factors on the transformation of Ukraine’s financial architecture. The directions for the transformation of Ukraine’s financial architecture, taking into account ESG factors and European benchmarks for sustainable finance, are presented. The research findings indicate that implementing sustainable development principles is not only a factor in modernizing Ukraine’s financial architecture but also a strategic tool for enhancing economic resilience, investment attractiveness, and international competitiveness. It is argued that building a financial architecture based on the principles of sustainable finance and the integration of ESG criteria is a necessary condition for attracting foreign investment as part of Ukraine’s post-war recovery.

title: Enterprise Informatics Capability and Manufacturing Supply Chain Resilience in the Digital Economy: The Roles of Information Transparency and Environmental Dynamism
summary: This study examines how enterprise informatics capability influences manufacturing supply chain resilience in the context of the digital economy.Drawing on organizational information processing theory and contingency theory, a moderated mediation model is developed to investigate the mediating role of information transparency and the moderating role of environmental dynamism.Survey data collected from 316 supply chain managers and senior executives in Chinese manufacturing firms are analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling.The findings indicate that enterprise informatics capability has a significant positive effect on manufacturing supply chain resilience both directly and indirectly through information transparency.Information transparency partially mediates this relationship by serving as a key information-transmission mechanism.Environmental dynamism does not significantly moderate the direct effect of enterprise informatics capability on supply chain resilience; however, it positively moderates the indirect effect through information transparency, such that the mediating pathway becomes stronger in highly dynamic environments.The findings contribute to the enterprise informatics literature by clarifying the information-processing pathways through which informatics capability translates into supply chain resilience, and by identifying the boundary conditions under which these pathways operate.Practical implications for manufacturing managers seeking to strengthen supply chain resilience through informatics investment are discussed.

title: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF ENTERPRISES IN THE POST-WAR PERIOD: LEGAL FOUNDATIONS OF ECONOMIC RECOVERY
summary: This article examines the legal foundations of sustainable enterprise development as a component of Ukraine’s economic recovery in the post-war period. It substantiates that rebuilding the enterprise sector cannot be limited to restoring destroyed production capacities and requires a modern legal environment capable of simultaneously ensuring investment attractiveness, financial and economic resilience, environmental responsibility, social inclusiveness, and sound corporate governance in line with European standards and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Legal regulation is considered an instrument of economic recovery and enterprise modernization through investment protection, financing and risk-sharing mechanisms, implementation of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) principles, support for digital transformation, and approximation of Ukrainian legislation to European Union law.The study is based on a systems approach and combines doctrinal, formal-legal, comparative legal, analytical, classification, conceptual modelling, multi-criteria evaluation, and Delphi expert methods. An integrated mathematical model for assessing the effectiveness of a comprehensive legal strategy for sustainable enterprise development is proposed. The model incorporates six interrelated components: regulatory and legal framework, institutional support, economic and legal incentives, digital legal support, social and environmental dimensions, and risk management and economic security. The weighting coefficients were determined using the Delphi method.The scientific novelty lies in developing an original conceptual model of a comprehensive legal strategy for ensuring sustainable enterprise development during Ukraine's post-war reconstruction. The proposed approach integrates legal, institutional, economic, digital, social, environmental, and security mechanisms into a unified framework. Unlike existing approaches, it combines legal regulation with ESG principles, digital transformation, economic security, risk management, and European integration, making it suitable for strategic planning, monitoring, and evaluating post-war recovery policies.The practical significance lies in the potential application of the proposed models by public authorities, business entities, international organizations, and development partners. Their implementation can contribute to strengthening investment attractiveness, competitiveness, economic resilience, and the integration of Ukrainian enterprises into the European economic area based on sustainable development.

title: Sustainable Supply Chain Economics and Global Market Adaptation Strategies
summary: The application of sustainable supply chain management is increasingly becoming a common approach for increasing efficiency, effectiveness, and resilience in an environment that is highly uncertain in terms of the global markets. In this research, the use of sustainable supply chain management approaches for the purpose of adaptation to the global market by means of green sourcing, resource efficiency, diversification of suppliers, regionalization, digital visibility, and flexibility is studied. An integrative conceptual framework is developed, linking the performance in sustainability to economic efficiency and supply chain resilience. The research further highlights the significance of regional adaptation and the adoption of circular practices as ways of minimizing costs and increasing competitiveness in the long run. The model proposed in this paper brings together all the elements needed to understand the interaction between sustainability and adaptation to global markets. The results indicate that organizations that combine environmental considerations with economic and adaptive competencies can increase supply reliability, decrease risk exposure, be more efficient with resources, and experience sustainable growth in their competitiveness.

title: Cybersecurity in the Digital Era: Implications for Financial Reporting and Audit
summary: This article examines cybersecurity as an emerging risk in financial reporting and financial audit, within a context shaped by the accelerated digitalisation of accounting systems and the increasing frequency of cyber incidents. The research adopts an integrated approach, combining theoretical analysis, bibliometric analysis, and an empirical investigation based on data concerning cybersecurity incidents. The objective of this research is to highlight the ways in which the digitalisation of financial reporting enhances the efficiency and quality of information, while simultaneously generating vulnerabilities that may affect the integrity and reliability of financial statements. The bibliometric analysis, conducted on a sample of 1,534 articles indexed in Web of Science (2015–2025), shows the consolidation of cybersecurity as an interdisciplinary field situated at the intersection of technology, governance, and audit. The empirical component uses data provided by Audit Analytics for 994 listed US companies over the period 2004–2025. The results indicate a concentration of attacks in economically and technologically developed regions, with personal and financial information as the main targets, and unauthorised access as the dominant attack method. The study confirms that cyber risks influence audit risk assessment, prompting auditors to intensify and diversify procedures to ensure the quality of financial information.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility in India: An Overview
summary: Abstract Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has emerged as an important mechanism for promoting social welfare and sustainable development in India. This paper provides an overview of the statutory framework governing CSR under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, including its applicability thresholds, expenditure requirements, committee structure, governance functions, reporting obligations, eligible activities under Schedule VII, and the treatment of unspent amounts. It also examines constitutional and ethical justifications for corporate responsibility, with particular reference to the right to life and a clean environment, the Polluter Pays Principle, and the relationship between business operations and stakeholder welfare. The paper highlights the role of CSR in supporting inclusive and sustainable development while noting the continuing importance of integrating environmental and social considerations into core business decisions.

title: Institutional Challenges and Digital Opportunities for Women Entrepreneurs
summary: Women Entrepreneurship is kind of a pillar that holds up global economic resilience, helps mix different kinds of jobs and somehow supports long-term social economic growth too. In today’s world Digital Transformation— driven by social commerce sites, cloud tools and new kinds of money tech— gives women founders fresh routes to get past older limits, mostly the ones that come from not having enough resources. Even so, there is still deep unfairness in the system. Biased ways of distributing funds, plus strict social rules keep slowing down the growth paths, and that part feels stubborn. This study builds a plan that looks at two sides, the help that comes from Digital Transformation, and the barriers that stay put. It zooms in on newer markets, for instance India. By using Institutional Theory and the 5Ms Framework, we can see how online shops, marketing efforts and FinTech money tools work like forces that lift Women Entrepreneurship. At the same time it checks why the digital gender gap stays around, why Capital Asymmetry keeps showing up in venture money decisions, and why work and home life clash for many women in daily reality. The study ends with evidence based policies that bring big economic players together with small businesses. The goal is to support the United Nations SDGs 5 and 8, and push Socio Economic Development so it can reach everyone.

summary: Este artículo propone un marco metodológico para el modelado del triple impacto mediante la convergencia analítica de estados financieros tradicionales y reportes de sustentabilidad. title: Digital Innovation and Its Impact on Business Transformation in the Modern Economy
summary: Abstract Digital innovation is a major catalyst providing the driving force in changing the modern business and economy. Technologies like AI, cloud computing, big data analytics, IoT, blockchain, and automation have transformed business operations, value creation, and customer interactions. Digital innovation goes beyond the introduction of new technologies: it also includes new product, services, processes and business models. This research paper explores the concept of digital innovation and how it's driving business transformation. It emphasises the key factors for digital innovation, technologies that enable digital innovation, the advantages for organisations, issues with implementing digital innovation and upcoming developments. The study is descriptive and exploratory research with the main method of collecting data from secondary data sources from academic journals, books, research reports and reliable sources on the internet. The study concludes that digital innovation can enhance operational efficiency, customer experience, productivity, decision making and competitiveness. But there are problems like cyber security threats, data privacy issues, cost of implementation, resistance to change and lack of digital skills in the organisations. The research findings show that organisations can reap the benefits of digital transformation successfully with the right strategies, staff and leadership, and the constant introduction of new ideas. The terms "Digital Innovation," "Digital Transformation," and "Artificial Intelligence" are all related to the concept of business transformation through technology. title: Identification and Validation of Components Affecting the Sustainability of the National Banking Network
summary: The present study was conducted with the aim of identifying and validating the components affecting the sustainability of the banking network, using both qualitative and quantitative phases. In the qualitative phase, a meta-synthesis approach was employed, and based on a systematic search of reputable scientific databases, 79 articles were identified. After applying the inclusion and exclusion criteria, 16 selected studies were analyzed. The findings of this phase indicated that in the economic and financial dimension, components such as operational efficiency and sustainable profitability, credit and liquidity risk management, capital adequacy and balance sheet structure, exposure to foreign exchange risk, and asset quality play a significant role in banking stability. In the institutional and corporate governance dimension, ownership structure, effective supervisory systems, and macroeconomic conditions were identified as key factors. In the technological dimension, components such as digital transformation, development of modern banking infrastructure, cybersecurity, and the use of artificial intelligence for risk management were found to be of particular importance. In the social dimension, banks’ social responsibility, transparency in communications, and enhancement of customer experience were identified as influential factors affecting public trust and social capital. In the quantitative phase, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was employed to validate the components extracted from the qualitative analysis. The results indicate that the sustainability of the banking network requires an integrated approach that simultaneously strengthens the economic, institutional, technological, and social dimensions.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A CONSTRUCTION SUPPLY CHAIN RESILIENCE MODEL FOR GIGA PROJECTS IN SAUDI ARABIA
summary: Saudi Arabias giga-project programmes create unusually demanding supply networks: complex project interfaces, geographically dispersed production, specialist imports, simultaneous demands for capacity and strict performance expectations. Although construction supply chain research increasingly addresses risk, digitisation and inter - firm collaboration, it offers limited guidance on how these capabilities should function as a coherent, project-level system under the conditions of large Saudi developments. This structured integrative review critically examines 30 peer-reviewed articles published between 2020 and 2025 and develops a context-sensitive Construction Supply Chain Resilience Model (CSCRM). Evidence is synthesised across disruption exposure, network configuration, procurement governance, operational visibility, adaptive execution and recovery learning. The proposed model connects five mutually dependent capabilities-exposure intelligence, protected sourcing, integrated information, adaptive delivery and institutional learning-through explicit decision rights and performance feedback.

title: Considerations Regarding the Reconfiguration of the Financial-Accounting Ecosystem in the Context of Modern Digital Technologies
summary: Recent digital transformations are redefining the way the financial-accounting ecosystem operates as a result of the integration of ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) systems and artificial intelligence in accounting, auditing and sustainability reporting processes. As a result of increasing transparency requirements, the adoption of European standards on sustainability reporting and the rapid development of the digital economy, organizations have had to intervene in the process of conducting business, by rethinking operational models and governance mechanisms. The article aims to analyze how the use of ERP systems and artificial intelligence can contribute to the reconfiguration of the financial-accounting ecosystem, facilitating augmented accounting, intelligent auditing and integrated reporting oriented towards economic, environmental and social performance. The objective of the paper is to identify the main opportunities and challenges generated by the integration of ERP systems and artificial intelligence in the financial and accounting activities undertaken by organizations, as well as to highlight the impact on the accounting profession and the decision-making process. The research method used to quantify the key findings relevant to the topic of this article was qualitative, focusing on the responses received from various respondents during interviews conducted with them. The results indicated a high degree of satisfaction of users in the financial-accounting field regarding the generation and analysis of financial and non-financial information, as well as the automation of repetitive activities, the detection of various anomalies and risks, and the monitoring of ESG indicators. The results also highlighted the standardization of data collection processes, the integration of financial and non-financial information into a single platform, the development of digital skills of accounting professionals and auditors, and the promotion of an organizational culture favorable to innovation and change. Thus, the study proposed in this article focuses on providing relevant information for both academia and practitioners or specialists in the financial-accounting and auditing fields regarding the building of intelligent, resilient and sustainable development-oriented organizations.

title: STATE POLICY ON BANKING REGULATION AMID THE DEVELOPMENT OF FINTECH TECHNOLOGIES AND GROWING DIGITAL RISKS TO NATIONAL SECURITY
summary: The purpose of the study is to examine the transformation of state regulation of banking activities in Ukraine in the context of the development of FinTech technologies and the intensification of digital risks, as well as to substantiate directions for improving the regulatory framework and banking supervision mechanisms, taking into account the requirements of financial stability and national security. The article substantiates that the digital transformation of the financial sector causes the modernization of banking services, contributes to increasing the efficiency of financial intermediation, expands financial inclusion, and ensures the development of innovative business models; however, it generates new challenges for the system of state regulation of banking activities, ensuring financial stability and cybersecurity. The principal trends in the digitalization of banking activities are identified, and the impact of FinTech technologies on the transformation of state regulatory mechanisms in the financial sector is characterized. The performance of Ukraine’s major banks — PrivatBank, Oschadbank, and Raiffeisen Bank — during 2022–2025 is analyzed, revealing growing trends toward the digitalization of banking operations, the expansion of remote service channels, an increase in the number of users of digital services, and a strengthening role of financial technologies in ensuring the competitiveness of banking institutions. It is established that, alongside the positive effects of digital transformation, cyber risks, digital fraud, data leakage, technological dependence on external platforms, and other threats affecting national security are increasing. The need to improve state banking regulation is substantiated through the development of RegTech and SupTech technologies, the introduction of risk-based digital supervision, stronger cyber resilience of banking infrastructure, improved digital-risk management mechanisms, and the harmonization of national legislation with European standards of digital financial regulation. It is demonstrated that an effective combination of innovative development in the financial sector and modern mechanisms of state oversight is a necessary prerequisite for ensuring financial stability and protecting national interests in the digital economy.

title: ESG DISCLOSURE PRACTICES AMONG EMERGING MARKET FIRMS: A CASE STUDY OF UZBEKISTAN

This article examines ESG disclosure practices among firms operating in Uzbekistan, focusing on the development of sustainability reporting, regulatory frameworks, corporate transparency, and the challenges faced by local enterprises. The study highlights the growing importance of environmental responsibility, social accountability, and effective governance in Uzbekistan’s transition towards a sustainable market economy. It also explores the role of international ESG standards, including the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) and International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), in improving the quality and comparability of corporate disclosures. The findings suggest that although ESG awareness is increasing among Uzbek companies, significant improvements are still needed in data collection, reporting consistency, independent verification, and stakeholder engagement.

title: FROM FINANCIAL REPORTING TO ALGORITHMIC REPORTING: EXPANDING THE SCOPE OF ACCOUNTABILITY IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: In the context of the rapidly evolving digital economy, data and algorithms are increasingly becoming critical drivers of enterprise value creation and operational efficiency. However, existing accounting and reporting systems continue to focus primarily on tangible assets and financial flows, thereby failing to adequately capture the role of digital assets and algorithmic models. This study employs a qualitative research approach based on a systematic literature review, comparative analysis of international regulatory frameworks, and secondary data analysis to examine the limitations of traditional financial reporting and explore the role of algorithm reporting in enhancing corporate accountability. The analysis focuses primarily on the Vietnamese context while drawing upon international governance experiences during the period 2019–2024, when AI adoption and digital transformation accelerated significantly. The study proposes an expansion of the scope of accountability from traditional financial reporting to algorithm reporting, with the aim of enhancing transparency, responsibility, and control within the digital economy. Theoretically, the study contributes to the emerging literature by extending the concept of accountability beyond financial disclosure to include algorithmic governance and digital resources. Practically, it proposes an integrated algorithm reporting framework and policy recommendations that support the modernization of accounting standards, AI governance, and auditing practices in Vietnam.

title: Investigation of the Impact of Digital Twin Technology on Strategic Supply Chain Resilience and Enterprise Operational Performance
summary: The turbulent global economy has witnessed abrupt fluctuations and repeated crises, fundamentally altering the operating modes of energy enterprises.Given recent environmental volatility, digital twin technology has emerged as a critical tool to enhance supply chain systems.Although conceptual studies on digitalization are abundant, empirical evidence detailing how digital twin technologies improve enterprise operations remains insufficient.Adopting the Dynamic Capabilities View, this paper establishes a moderated mediation model and conducts empirical research using a stratified sample of 342 senior operating managers and supply chain directors in the energy sector.Using partial least squares structural equation modeling, the empirical results indicate that digital twin technologies directly promote the improvement of operational performance.Furthermore, strategic supply chain resilience partially mediates this relationship.Additionally, the results demonstrate that environmental dynamism moderates these indirect paths; notably, the strategic value of digital twin technology is amplified under conditions of high market volatility.This study provides new theoretical support for supply chain management and offers a practical model for managers to build resilience and improve performance in high-volatility environments.

title: The Effects of Corporate Social Responsibility and Good Corporate Governance on Firm Value, with Profitability as a Moderating Variable
summary: This study examines the effect of corporate social responsibility (CSR) disclosure, managerial ownership, and institutional ownership on firm value, with profitability (ROA) as a moderating variable, in food and beverage companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. Using a purposive sample of 16 firms (80 firm-year observations) and panel data regression with the Fixed Effects Model, the results show that CSR disclosure has a significant negative effect on firm value (β = −0.416802, p = 0.0095), managerial ownership has a significant positive effect (β = 0.155062, p = 0.0026), while institutional ownership shows no significant effect (β = −2.035018, p = 0.2957). CSR, managerial ownership, and institutional ownership jointly affect firm value (F = 10.99921, p = 0.000000, adjusted R² = 0.706303). Profitability significantly moderates the CSR–firm value relationship (β = 0.015940, p = 0.0358): because the CSR main effect is negative (β = −0.416802), this positive interaction indicates that profitability offsets part of the negative CSR effect rather than reversing it. Profitability does not significantly moderate the effect of managerial or institutional ownership on firm value. This study contributes to the CSR–firm value literature by distinguishing an offsetting moderation pattern from a reinforcing one, within a single sector (food and beverage) and post-pandemic period (2020–2024) not extensively covered in prior moderation studies.

summary: This study aims to examine and analyze the effect of good corporate governance mechanism, financial performance, growth opportunity, and ESG disclosure on firm value. The data used are secondary data obtained from the annual reports and sustainability reports of IDX30 companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The analysis method used in this study is panel data regression analysis using the EViews 13 software. The result of this study show that leverage, ESG disclosure, and firm size have an effect on firm value. Meanwhile, managerial ownership, institutional ownership, profitability, and growth opportunity do not have an effect on firm value.

title: From Satellite Availability to Financial Information: An Auditable Sentinel-1B Benchmark
summary: This paper examines whether satellite observation availability translates into useful economic information, using the December 2021 interruption of Sentinel-1B as a case study. The analysis links 176 mining sites and 38 listed issuers with public satellite acquisition records, administrative production data, radar measurements, and verified corporate disclosure dates. Across 175 sites with defined exposure, reliance on Sentinel-1B was highly stable between 2020 and 2021 but only modestly correlated with realized coverage loss in 2022. Additional Sentinel-1A observations offset 28.6% of the mechanical loss of B-only observation dates. A separate pilot containing 2,043 radar site-scene measurements supports 319 retrospective test point-quarters. Adding Sentinel-1B features did not improve mean squared production-estimation error in any annual test fold. Financial diagnostics covering 572 disclosures also reveal pre-event trends that prevent a clean causal interpretation. The paper documents the methods, results, and measurement limitations involved in connecting satellite data to economic outcomes. It provides a benchmark for evaluating alternative-data signals without assuming that additional imagery necessarily improves prediction or identifies a market effect. title: Making time through climate finance: temporal rationalities and practices of the Green Climate Fund in Vanuatu
summary: The climate crisis is a crisis of ordering and governing time. This paper interrogates how multilateral climate finance relies upon, and reinforces, particular temporal regimes and imaginaries around the relationship between modernity, coloniality, and time. Specifically, it asks: which temporal rationalities are inscribed in, and which structured temporal practices are enacted through the climate finance regime in Vanuatu, and beyond? Based on an ethnographic document analysis of funding proposals and investment criteria of the Green Climate Fund, I argue that the GCF actively governs ni-Vanuatu communities through time. Through different notions of (colonial) temporality informed by Pasifika political ecology scholarship, this paper explores the impact of these funding schemes in negotiating climatic futures. Methodologically, it approaches the GCF’s document machine as a social agent that diagnoses presents, anticipates futures, and renders particular interventions viable over others. The paper shows that the Green Climate Fund is not merely a mechanism for transferring resources; it is a temporal governance regime that diagnoses presents as deficient, renders futures governable, and thereby structures which Pacific futures become legible and investable. By foregrounding temporality, this study contributes to ongoing debates on climate coloniality and the political economy of delay, while situating Vanuatu as a critical site to rethink how power operates across scales, spaces, and times.

title: The Integrative Role of the Audit Committee in Coordinating Internal Audit and External Audit
summary: This study examines the integrative role of the audit committee in coordinating internal audit and external audit functions within corporate governance systems. Although the academic literature has extensively analysed these assurance mechanisms, they are typically studied separately, and the conceptualisation of the audit committee as a coordination interface between them remains underdeveloped. The research employs the Structured Literature Review (SLR) methodology, following the framework proposed by Massaro et al. (2016), to ensure transparency and rigour in the selection and synthesis of existing studies. Starting from an initial set of 310 articles indexed in the Web of Science database, a multi-stage filtering process led to a final sample of 25 relevant studies, of which 17 directly analyse the interaction among internal audit, external audit, and the audit committee. The results reveal the predominance of a structural monitoring perspective, with most studies analysing bilateral relationships between the audit committee and one of the two audit functions. Trilateral approaches that simultaneously integrate all three governance mechanisms remain limited. Based on the synthesis conducted, the study proposes a conceptual framework structured around three levels — structural inputs, integration mechanisms, and governance outcomes — which positions the audit committee as an active interface facilitating coordination between internal audit and external audit. The main contribution of the research lies in integrating fragmented streams of the specialised literature and in developing a conceptual model that highlights the potential integrative role of the audit committee in the assurance architecture, while also providing a basis for future empirical testing.

title: The impact of Digital Economy on Economic Growth in India
summary: Abstract The digital economy has turned out to be a major contributor to India's economic transformation and growth. The digitalisation of business, government, and consumers has changed the way they interact, with speedy progress in digital technologies, internet penetration, digital payments, e-commerce, and digital public infrastructure (DPI). This study explores the effects of the digital economy on the economic growth of India and specifically on productivity, job creation, financial inclusion, entrepreneurship and innovation. The initiatives like Digital India, Unified Payments Interface (UPI), and the digital banking are helping in economic participation and better access to financial and public services. However, the rise of digital platforms has also opened up opportunities for small businesses and entrepreneurs to reach larger markets and lower transaction fees. There are however challenges that are hindering the inclusive benefits of digitalisation, including the digital divide, the threat of cyber-security, the issue of data privacy, insufficient digital literacy, and unequal access to digital infrastructure. The study finds digital economy has great potential to boost India's economic growth and competitiveness. Development of digital skills, inclusive access to technology, strengthening digital infrastructure and securing cyber security are key to sustainable and inclusive economic growth in India.

title: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF CASH HOLDINGS IN THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND FIRM VALUE: EVIDENCE FROM LISTED SERVICE FIRMS
summary: This study examines the relationship between corporate governance, cash holdings, and firm value among listed service firms in Vietnam. The rapid development of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and financial technology (FinTech), has brought new demands for financial flexibility and corporate governance, particularly in the service sector. This raises an important question of whether firms' cash holding decisions provide a link between corporate governance and firm value. The analysis is based on panel data collected from service firms listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HOSE) and the Hanoi Stock Exchange (HNX) from 2020 to 2024. Corporate governance is measured using five governance characteristics, including board size, board independence, CEO duality, board gender diversity, and foreign ownership. Firm value is proxied by Tobin's Q, while cash holdings are measured as the ratio of cash and cash equivalents to total assets. The empirical procedure involves fixed-effects and random-effects estimations and the Hausman test. FGLS is used after diagnostic tests identify heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation, while the indirect effects are tested using bootstrap analysis. The results are not uniform across the five governance characteristics. CEO duality is positively associated with cash holdings, whereas board gender diversity and foreign ownership are positively associated with firm value. No significant relationship is found between cash holdings and firm value, and the bootstrap results do not support the mediating role of cash holdings. Thus, for the firms in the sample, the evidence points to direct relationships between specific governance characteristics and firm value rather than an indirect relationship through cash holdings. The study adds evidence from Vietnamese listed service firms, a setting that has received relatively limited attention in research on the governance–cash–value relationship. The results also underline the relevance of board composition and ownership structure when firms and policymakers consider measures to improve corporate governance.

title: Community Empowerment Education through Corporate Social Responsibility Programs: Strengthening Entrepreneurial Capacity and Sustainable Socio-Economic Independence
summary: This study aims to analyze the implementation strategy of PT Inkorincorp Velocity's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program in empowering local communities, channeling its impact on capacity building and independence of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) actors, and identifying development synergies built in Balikpapan City. This study uses a qualitative descriptive approach with a case study design. Data was collected through in-depth interviews with CSR management, local governments, and target MSME actors, which were strengthened by field observations and documentation studies. Data analysis was carried out using the interactive model Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña with data validity tests through triangulation of sources and techniques. The results of the study show that PT Inkorincorp Velocity applies an empowerment approach based on participatory needs assessment that changes the CSR paradigm from charitable philanthropy to sustainable community building. The implications of the program can be seen in increasing turnover, expanding digital market reach, as well as strengthening social capital and institutional independence of citizen business groups. In addition, the realization of the synergy of the Triple Helix partnership between the company, the Balikpapan City Government, and the local community that not only encourages inclusive economic growth but also strengthens the company's social license to operate. The study concludes that structured CSR integration programs with local potential are effective in transforming socio-economic vulnerabilities into competitive community self-reliance.

title: Green Investment, Environmental, Social and Governance Disclosures, and Corporate Social Responsibility: The Case of Nigerian Companies
summary: Existing research provides little evidence that investments with an environmental focus promote better corporate social responsibility (CSR) practices or are simply symbolic actions in weak institutional environments. Hence, this study investigated the effect of green investment and ESG disclosures on the CSR performance of listed companies in Nigeria. The research was grounded in stakeholder and institutional theories to explain the relationship between environmentally driven investments and corporate social outcomes. Secondary data was collected from annual reports of selected listed companies for ten years and analysed using the Feasible Generalised Least Squares (FGLS) and Driscoll-Kraay Standard Error (DKSE) estimation techniques. The findings revealed that green investment has a positive and significant impact on CSR practices (Z = 4.849, p < 0.01). This implies that companies with higher green investment practices have more participation in environmental protection, community development, and responsible governance. The results also suggested that supporting factors such as green capital expenditure, ESG initiatives, green technological innovation, and carbon emission reduction efforts have an influence on the success of green investment. The study found that green investment improves CSR performance; however, its effect may be reduced to a legitimacy tool where institutional structures are weak. The research indicates that policymakers should tighten sustainability regulations and foster transparent ESG reporting. At the same time, companies should connect green investment to long-term environmental and social strategies to achieve meaningful CSR outcomes.

title: FINANCIAL TRANSPARENCY PRACTICES IN CONSTRUCTION COMPANIES: CHALLENGES AND DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES (THE CASE OF GEORGIA)
summary: Financial transparency is one of the most important principles of modern corporate governance and sustainable business development, particularly in capital-intensive sectors characterized by a high level of financial risk, such as the construction industry. This study aims to examine the practices of financial transparency in Georgian construction companies, identify existing challenges, and assess opportunities for improvement. The paper discusses the theoretical foundations of financial transparency and explores its role in corporate governance, the formation of a favorable investment environment, and the enhancement of organizational effectiveness. The research is based on an analysis of international academic literature, recommendations of international organizations, International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), statistical data from Georgia, and recent trends in the development of the construction sector. Particular attention is paid to the specific characteristics of the construction industry, including long-term projects, large-scale investment flows, multi-stage contractual arrangements, and the complexities associated with managing extensive subcontractor networks, all of which increase the necessity for financial transparency. The study identifies several major challenges facing the Georgian construction sector, including insufficient financial disclosure, underdeveloped corporate governance mechanisms, limited adoption of digital technologies and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems, and issues related to investor confidence. At the same time, the paper highlights significant opportunities for enhancing financial transparency through the comprehensive implementation of IFRS, the strengthening of audit institutions, the integration of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting practices, and the adoption of modern digital financial management systems. The findings indicate that a high level of financial transparency significantly increases investor confidence, improves the efficiency of financial resource management, reduces corruption and operational risks, facilitates the attraction of foreign investment, and strengthens the competitiveness of construction companies in both domestic and international markets. Therefore, the development of financial transparency mechanisms represents a critical prerequisite for the sustainable growth and long-term economic development of Georgia’s construction sector.

title: ESG Disclosure and Firm Profitability: The Moderating Roles of Firm Size and Corporate Governance
summary: The disclosure of Environmental, Social, and Governance practices has gained prominence as companies encounter heightened expectations from investors, regulators, and various stakeholders for enhanced transparency regarding their ESG activities. This study investigates the correlation between ESG disclosure and corporate profitability, focusing specifically on the moderating influence of company size. The study employs a quantitative methodology and uses purposive sampling to obtain 310 firm-year data points. Information was acquired via publicly accessible annual reports, sustainability documents, and ESG data sources. Corporate profitability is assessed using return on assets (ROA), whereas ESG transparency serves as the primary explanatory variable. The size of the firm is analyzed as a moderating variable, while firm age, leverage, revenue, and market capitalization are considered as control factors. Pearson correlation and moderated regression analysis were used to investigate the proposed relationships. The results indicate a negative and statistically significant correlation between ESG disclosure and profitability. The regression findings indicate a negative correlation between ESG disclosure and ROA (β = −0.116; t = −3.331), failing to substantiate the claim that ESG disclosure enhances profitability. The negative correlation persists as significant even after incorporating firm size into the model (β = −0.117; t = −3.245). The relationship between ESG disclosure and firm size is both positive and statistically significant (β = 0.118; t = 2.768), suggesting that firm size influences the ESG–profitability relationship. The negative correlation between ESG disclosure and profitability decrease with the growth of corporate size. The results indicate that the economic impacts of ESG disclosure vary among companies. Increased ESG disclosure correlates with decreased short-term accounting profitability; however, larger corporations seem more capable of managing the costs linked to ESG implementation and reporting, thereby mitigating negative profitability effects. The research thus illustrates that the size of a corporation is a significant variable in understanding the ESG–profitability relationship. The results bear significance for corporate executives, investors, and regulators. Managers must include ESG initiatives in overarching financial and operational strategies instead of regarding ESG disclosure as an isolated compliance task.

title: Dampak Kesulitan Keuangan terhadap Indikasi Praktik Greenwashing: Analisis Peran Mediasi Inovasi Hijau
summary: Greenwashing has become a critical issue in corporate sustainability implementation; however, research on the impact of financial distress on greenwashing remains limited and yields inconsistent results. This study addresses this gap by examining the role of green innovation as a mediating variable in the relationship between financial distress and greenwashing, drawing upon legitimacy theory and stakeholder theory. The study focuses on energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange from 2020 to 2024, utilizing a sample of 87 companies (comprising 267 observations after outlier removal). Secondary data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and path analysis. The results indicate that financial distress has no significant effect on either greenwashing indications or green innovation. Similarly, green innovation does not significantly affect greenwashing indications. Conversely, firm size was found to have a significant positive effect on greenwashing indications. title: ESG INFORMATION DISCLOSURE AND CORPORATE FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE: A LITERATURE REVIEW
summary: The study presents a systematic review that investigates the interplay between corporate ESG information disclosure and corporate financial performance. Following the PRISMA framework, the paper uses a systematic literature review methodology to ensure rigor, standardization and transparency throughout the research process. Literature was sourced from the Web of Science and Scopus databases based on structured keyword clusters pertaining to ESG information disclosure, corporate financial performance and corporate operational behavior. After screening the initially retrieved records against unified inclusion and exclusion criteria, 51 eligible academic studies were selected for thematic analysis and systematic synthesis. A standardized coding matrix was used to extract and organize core research variables such as ESG disclosure quality, disclosure dimensions, corporate profitability, operational efficiency and market performance. The findings show that high-quality ESG information disclosure significantly enhances corporate financial performance by reducing corporate financing constraints, alleviating information asymmetry, and building corporate stakeholder trust. The economic effects of ESG disclosure vary considerably depending on factors such as enterprise property rights, industry attributes and regional institutional environments. In addition, internal corporate governance and external market supervision serve as critical moderating variables in the influencing mechanism. By examining both positive and negative correlations as well as nonlinear relationships reported in existing studies, this review brings clarity to prevailing research contradictions and theoretical gaps. The results carry practical implications for corporate sustainable operation, standardized ESG information disclosure and capital market supervision. Theoretically, this study contributes to stakeholder theory, signal transmission theory and sustainable development theory as applied within corporate financial management.

title: Role of Digital Banking and Fintech in Enhancing Financial Inclusion
summary: Abstract Digital banking and FinTech have emerged as crucial mechanisms to support financial inclusion by minimising the transactional, geographical and infrastructural barriers to conventional financial services. This paper investigates the contribution of digital banking and financial technology to enhance financial accessibility, service quality and affordability while recognising the vital factors that support financial inclusion. This study has drawn on a literature review and theoretical interpretation to demonstrate the contribution of digital banking and FinTech to exclusive financial inclusion. This paper adopted an interpretivist philosophy, exploratory design, and deductive approach to synthesise the peer-reviewed secondary evidence that was published recently. The methodological stance supported comparing and contrasting recurring themes in the existing literature. The findings of the study highlight the capacity of FinTech to increase financial inclusion; however, barriers like poor connectivity, lack of digital literacy, use of trust and regulatory complexities are restricting the financial inclusion. Overall, digital banking services and FinTech, including a suitable regulatory framework, can strengthen financial inclusion.

summary: The article aims to substantiate the role and define the functional capabilities of information-analytical decision support systems in international investment within the context of digital transformation, as well as to systematize the modern digital tools, analytical methods, and information components that facilitate the preparation and making of investment decisions. Achieving this goal involves examining the interrelationships among digital data sources, analytical technologies, forecasting and risk assessment mechanisms, and investment outcomes. The study systematizes modern digital technologies and information resources used in decision support systems for international investment, outlining their functional purposes; analyzes the systems' capabilities regarding data collection and integration, investment attractiveness assessment, market indicator forecasting, risk identification, and the modeling of alternative international investment scenarios; and substantiates a structural-functional model for the information-analytical support of international investment decisions, defining the connections between data sources, analytical tools, digital technologies, and decision outcomes. Furthermore, the article makes a theoretical and practical contribution to enhancing the soundness, timeliness, and adaptability of international investment decisions by integrating modern digital technologies, information resources, and analytical tools into a unified information-analytical decision support system. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the refinement of the functional-structural approach to the information-analytical support of international investment decisions through the systematization of digital technologies and analytical tools based on their roles in data collection, assessment, forecasting, risk analysis, and the formulation of investment alternatives. A structural-functional model of adaptive information-analytical support is proposed, integrating data sources, digital technologies, analytical procedures, investment decision-making mechanisms, and feedback into a single closed-loop system.

title: Beyond compliance: Embedding ethics in ESG reform for emerging economies
summary: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reforms are expanding across emerging economies, yet many initiatives struggle to achieve ethical legitimacy in practice. Prior research has emphasized the adoption of disclosure and the development of metrics, while offering a limited explanation of why ESG systems often remain vulnerable to symbolic compliance, exclusion, and trust deficits in institutionally constrained contexts. The study addresses this gap by examining how structural conditions shape the ethical quality of ESG governance, particularly in relation to fairness, accountability, legitimacy, inclusion, and rights. A qualitative, interpretive design was adopted, drawing on the analysis of 56 publicly available documents, including corporate ESG disclosures, regulatory and policy frameworks, and civil society assessments. NVivo-assisted thematic coding integrates ethics-informed deductive categories with inductive theme development to identify recurring barriers and their normative implications. The findings indicate that fragmented mandates create compliance ambiguity and privilege well-resourced incumbents, while weak enforcement mechanisms enable disclosure without substantive accountability. Trust deficits among investors, regulators, and local communities further undermine legitimacy, especially where stakeholder engagement is perceived as formalistic. In addition, infrastructure and data limitations restrict participation by smaller actors, and the growing digitization of ESG systems introduces under-regulated risks related to privacy and algorithmic opacity. The study reframes ESG reform in emerging economies as an ethical governance challenge and identifies adaptive pathways for building more credible, inclusive, and ethically robust ESG systems.

title: REGULATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN FINTECH SECTOR: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES IN INDONESIA
summary: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly influenced various sectors, including financial technology (fintech). In Indonesia, fintech innovations such as digital payments and wealth management are reshaping financial services. However, the regulatory framework for AI in this sector remains underdeveloped, creating both challenges and opportunities. This article explores the current state of AI regulation in Indonesia's fintech sector and examines the potential hurdles and benefits of implementing comprehensive AI regulations. Utilizing a normative juridical approach, the study integrates conceptual, statutory, and case-based analyses to provide a multidimensional understanding of the issue. The findings reveal several challenges, including algorithmic bias, data privacy concerns, and the complexity of ensuring transparency and accountability in AI-based decision-making. On the other hand, AI offers opportunities for increased efficiency, enhanced risk assessment, and improved financial services scalability. The article underscores the urgency of establishing specific regulations to ensure AI accountability and transparency while fostering innovation. Such measures will help Indonesia balance the benefits of AI integration in fintech with the need to safeguard legal and ethical standards.

title: DEVELOPMENT, TRANSLATION AND PRELIMINARY VALIDATION OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND GREEN LOGISTICS MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT
summary: This study develops, translates, and preliminarily validates a measurement instrument designed to assess digital transformation–driven green logistics practices and sustainability within cross-cultural logistics environments. A multi-phase methodological framework was applied, beginning with the conceptualization of constructs and the systematic generation of items based on established literature. Content and face validity were confirmed through expert evaluations, yielding strong CVI scores and demonstrating item relevance, clarity, and representativeness. The instrument was translated using standardized forward–backward procedures, followed by expert committee review to ensure semantic and conceptual equivalence. Cognitive debriefing further verified respondent comprehension, while a pilot test involving 30 logistics professionals provided evidence of acceptable internal consistency and survey feasibility. Structural validation procedures, such as Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), were intentionally deferred due to the small pilot sample size. Although the present study produced an Arabic version, the development and adaptation processes followed internationally recognized standards, making the instrument suitable for application in other linguistic and cultural contexts with appropriate adaptation. Overall, the study delivers a culturally attuned and conceptually robust pre-final instrument that lays the groundwork for future large-scale psychometric validation and empirical investigations into the role of digital transformation in advancing sustainable logistics practices.

title: Design and Validation of a Performance Improvement Model Based on Social Responsibility Accounting
summary: The present study was conducted with the aim of designing and validating a performance improvement model based on social responsibility accounting in companies listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange. This research employed an exploratory mixed-methods approach implemented in two qualitative and quantitative phases. In the qualitative phase, using thematic analysis and semi-structured interviews with 20 theoretical and practical experts, the dimensions, components, and indicators of the model were identified. Test–retest reliability with a coefficient of 69% and intra-subject agreement between two coders confirmed the analytical rigor of this phase. In the quantitative phase, the extracted model was validated with the participation of 245 financial managers from listed companies using a 68-item questionnaire and structural equation modeling based on the partial least squares (PLS-SEM) approach. The findings indicated that the final model consisted of six principal constructs: “Corporate Social Accountability,” “Social Transparency and Disclosure,” “Accounting Identification and Measurement of Environmental Impacts,” “Environmental Accounting Reporting and Disclosure,” “Financial Performance,” and “Non-Financial Performance.” The path analysis results demonstrated the positive and significant effects of social accounting (path coefficient = 0.517) and environmental accounting (path coefficient = 0.715) on organizational performance. The coefficient of determination (R²) showed that these two paths jointly explained 72% of the variance in performance. Furthermore, hierarchical analysis ranked the dimensions, with “Social Transparency and Disclosure” and “Environmental Reporting” receiving the highest priorities, respectively. The satisfactory fit of the model was confirmed by a GOF index of 0.620 and an NFI value of 0.957. In addition, the internal and external validity of the model was endorsed by experts, with mean scores exceeding 4.20. The proposed model provides an operational framework for integrating social and environmental commitments into organizational performance management systems.

title: INTELLECTUAL CAPITAL MODERATES FINANCIAL EFFICIENCY AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION WITH SUSTAINABLE GROWTH RATE
summary: This study aimed to examine the effect of financial efficiency and digital transformation on the sustainable growth rate, with intellectual capital as a moderating variable, in non-cyclical consumer companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2021–2024 period. The study employed a quantitative approach with a causal-associative design. The population consisted of 131 non-cyclical consumer companies, and a sample of 50 companies was selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 200 firm-year observations over four years. Secondary data were collected from annual reports published on the Indonesia Stock Exchange website. The data were analyzed using panel data regression and Moderated Regression Analysis with the assistance of EViews 13. The results showed that financial efficiency had no significant effect on the sustainable growth rate, with a regression coefficient of −0.358 and a significance value of 0.379. Digital transformation had a significant positive effect on the sustainable growth rate, with a regression coefficient of 0.022 and a significance value of 0.040. Intellectual capital did not moderate the relationship between financial efficiency and the sustainable growth rate, with a significance value of 0.486, nor the relationship between digital transformation and the sustainable growth rate, with a significance value of 0.190. The F-test confirmed that financial efficiency and digital transformation simultaneously affected the sustainable growth rate with a significance value of 0.048. These findings implied that digital transformation served as a key driver of sustainable growth, while financial efficiency and intellectual capital did not strengthen the sustainable growth rate in the non-cyclical consumer sector during the study period.

title: DETERMINANT OF THE MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING EFFECTIVENESS IN TOURISM FIRMS
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI), rising customer demand for individualized services, and growing need to strike a balance between rising operating costs and service quality are all driving the tourism industry's rapid digital transformation. Effective management accounting systems are now more crucial than ever for facilitating managerial decision-making, boosting organizational competitiveness, and increasing operational efficiency. There is no empirical data on how organizational skills and AI-related investment considerations together affect management accounting effectiveness in tourism businesses, especially in emerging nations, despite the increased focus on digital transformation. This study looks into how management accounting effectiveness in Vietnamese tourism businesses is affected by top management support, accounting staff competency, and AI adoption costs. The study used a sequential research approach that included expert interviews, a pilot survey, and a large-scale quantitative survey. It was based on the Resource-Based View and Contingency Theory. Reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, multiple regression analysis, and Pearson correlation analysis were used to examine the gathered data. The empirical results show that while top management support does not show a statistically significant direct effect, accounting staff competency and AI implementation cost positively and considerably influence management accounting effectiveness. These results imply that, rather than relying solely on managerial dedication, successful management accounting in tourism-related businesses increasingly requires organizational capacities able to combine professional accounting knowledge with commercially viable AI investments. By applying the Resource-Based View and Contingency Theory to the setting of digitally evolving tourism businesses in an emerging economy, the study adds to the body of knowledge in management accounting. In an increasingly competitive and technologically advanced business environment, the findings also have practical implications for tourism managers looking to improve managerial decision-making through accounting human capital development, strategically managed AI implementation, and long-term organizational capability building.

title: Thin capitalization and tax avoidance: The moderating role of independent commissioners
summary: This study examines the effect of thin capitalization on tax avoidance and the moderating role of independent commissioners in consumer non-cyclical companies in Indonesia. The study employs 150 firm-year observations from companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021-2023. The hypotheses are tested using fixed-effects panel regression estimated via Generalized Least Squares (GLS) to address heteroskedasticity. The results indicate that thin capitalization has a positive effect on tax avoidance, while independent commissioners weaken this relationship. These findings suggest that debt financing provides firms with opportunities to reduce their tax burdens through interest deductions. In contrast, greater representation of independent commissioners may constrain the tax-related implications of financing decisions. This study contributes to the literature by highlighting the role of corporate governance in moderating the relationship between thin capitalization and tax avoidance. The findings also provide implications for the Directorate General of Taxes in strengthening risk-based supervision of debt-related tax deductions and corporate financing arrangements.
