title: THE MEDIATING FUNCTION OF PERCEIVED CREDIBILITY IN THE IMPACT OF SUSTAINABILITY REPORT QUALITY ON INVESTOR TRUST
summary: This study examines the relationship between investor trust and perceived sustainability reporting quality, paying special attention to the mediating function of perceived credibility. The study creates an integrated framework based on signaling theory and information asymmetry theory to explain how investors understand sustainability disclosures and convert their evaluations into trust in reporting firms. In particular, the study looks at the direct connections between investor trust, perceived sustainability reporting quality, and perceived credibility. It also evaluates whether credibility may explain the relationship between investor confidence and reporting quality. Individual investors and representatives of institutional investors in Vietnam provided survey data. With investor type included as a control variable and bootstrapping used to assess the mediating link, covariance-based structural equation modeling was used to analyze the suggested correlations. The results show that investor trust and perceived credibility are positively correlated with higher perceived sustainability reporting quality. Additionally, investor trust and perceived credibility are positively correlated, and the relationship between reporting quality and trust is partially mediated by perceived credibility. These results imply that sustainability disclosures boost investor confidence by increasing the credibility that investors assign to company information in addition to its perceived quality. The scientific uniqueness of the study is the identification of perceived credibility as a unique explanatory mechanism that links investor trust in an emerging capital market with sustainability reporting quality. The study expands on current debates on sustainability disclosure and investor decision-making by combining reporting quality, credibility, and investor trust under a single empirical paradigm. Practically speaking, the results highlight the significance of transparent, consistent, comparable, and verifiable sustainability information in boosting investor confidence and corporate communication, especially as digital technologies increasingly influence access to sustainability-related information.

title: Pengaruh Retained Earnings, Debt Capacity, dan Operational Efficiency terhadap Firm Value dengan Macroeconomic Stability sebagai Variabel Moderating pada Perusahaan Food and Beverage yang Terdaftar di BEI Periode 2021–2025
summary: The objective of this inquiry is to evaluate how corporate value responds to internal financial allocations, borrowing thresholds, and resource utilization, while considering how country-level price stability alters these interactions. The empirical focus centers on the consumer goods sector, specifically food and drink operations, within the Indonesian capital market from 2021 to 2025. Employing a numerical strategy, this framework processes historical information gathered from corporate annual updates and public cost-of-living metrics. A deliberate selection criterion narrowed the scope to half a dozen entities, yielding thirty distinct data points. Market valuation is evaluated through the equity-to-book metric, whereas overall price consistency is measured via the shifting cost of consumer goods. Methodologically, the architecture utilizes longitudinal data systems combined with interactive regression structures. The evidence indicates that corporate wealth appreciation is driven primarily by internal profit accumulation. Conversely, borrowing thresholds, operational speed, and broader monetary environments show no meaningful connection to market worth. Furthermore, wider price stability fails to alter the connections between these internal metrics and market valuation. Ultimately, sector-specific market worth reacts far more to domestic earnings management than to general market price shifts.

title: Pengaruh Tax Transparency dan ESG Disclosure terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pada Perusahaan Manufaktur di Indonesia
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh transparansi perpajakan (tax transparency) dan pengungkapan Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) terhadap nilai perusahaan manufaktur di Indonesia. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain eksplanatori dan metode cross-sectional. Data primer diperoleh melalui penyebaran kuesioner kepada 125 responden yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Pengukuran variabel menggunakan skala Likert lima poin, sedangkan analisis data dilakukan melalui regresi linear berganda dengan bantuan perangkat lunak SPSS versi 25. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa transparansi perpajakan memiliki hubungan positif dan signifikan dengan nilai perusahaan, dengan koefisien regresi sebesar 0,562 dan signifikansi < 0,001. Pengungkapan ESG juga menunjukkan hubungan positif dan signifikan dengan koefisien regresi sebesar 0,412 dan signifikansi < 0,001. Secara simultan, kedua variabel menunjukkan hubungan yang signifikan dengan nilai perusahaan berdasarkan nilai F sebesar 52,811 dan signifikansi < 0,001. Nilai koefisien determinasi sebesar 0,464 menunjukkan bahwa transparansi perpajakan dan pengungkapan ESG mampu menjelaskan 46,4% variasi nilai perusahaan yang dipersepsikan. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa transparansi perpajakan dan pengungkapan ESG merupakan faktor penting yang berkaitan dengan penilaian positif terhadap nilai perusahaan. Temuan ini memberikan implikasi bagi manajemen perusahaan untuk meningkatkan akuntabilitas, kualitas pengungkapan informasi, dan penerapan prinsip keberlanjutan guna memperkuat kepercayaan pemangku kepentingan.

title: Digital Transformation and Organizational Performance: An Empirical Study of Selected Indian Organizations
summary: Abstract Digital transformation has emerged as an important strategic priority for organizations seeking to improve operational efficiency, innovation, customer experience and overall organizational performance. The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, data analytics, automation and digital platforms has significantly changed the way organizations operate and make managerial decisions. This study examines the relationship between digital transformation and organizational performance in selected Indian organizations. The study focuses on major dimensions of digital transformation, including digital technology adoption, cloud computing, artificial intelligence and automation, data analytics, digital platforms, and digital capabilities of employees. Organizational performance is examined in terms of operational efficiency, employee productivity, innovation, customer satisfaction and business performance. The study adopts a quantitative research design and proposes the collection of primary data through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation and regression analysis are proposed for testing the relationship between digital transformation and organizational performance. The study is expected to provide useful insights for managers and organizations regarding the role of digital technologies in improving organizational outcomes.

title: Analysis of Digital Literacy and the Readiness of MSMEs in Setupatok Village in Facing Digital Transformation
summary: Digital transformation is a major challenge for traditional micro enterprises, yet village level MSMEs are rarely captured in national digitalization statistics. This study aims to describe the level of digital literacy, the level of readiness for digital transformation, and the barriers to digital adoption among micro enterprises in Setupatok Village, Mundu District, Cirebon Regency. A descriptive mixed methods design was used. Fifteen MSME actors from five trading and culinary business types were selected purposively. Data were collected through a ten item Likert questionnaire covering five digital literacy indicators and five readiness indicators derived from the Technology Readiness Index, complemented by open ended questions and on site interviews. Questionnaire data were tabulated into frequencies, percentages, and mean scores, while interview data were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman interactive model. The results show that digital literacy is at a low to basic level (mean 2.45 of 5.00); 11 of 15 respondents (73.3%) disagreed that they use Google Maps or Google Business Profile, and 10 respondents (66.7%) disagreed that they accept QRIS payments. Readiness is also low (mean 2.56): discomfort and insecurity scores were high, while optimism and innovativeness were moderate. The main barriers are limited device and internet access, low technological understanding, distrust of non cash payment security, age and habit factors, and the absence of continuous mentoring. The study concludes that rural micro enterprises are still at an early stage of digital transformation and require practice based, continuous mentoring rather than one way socialization.

title: Cybersecurity as a Fiduciary Duty in Corporate Governance: Directors' Obligations Regarding Corporate Data Breaches in India
summary: As Indian companies rely more and more on digital technology, Cybersecurity has grown from a technical concern into a key component of corporate governance. Corporate data breaches can cause business disruption, compromise of personal data, loss of investor confidence, and regulatory and financial liabilities. This article examines whether cybersecurity ought to be a fiduciary duty of directors in India. This article examines various provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, directions issued by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Even though Indian law contains no explicit provision making cybersecurity a fiduciary duty, directors are subject to several duties that can be used to hold them accountable, including the duty of care, the duty of diligence, the duty of risk management, and the duty of legal compliance. It can therefore be concluded that effective corporate governance will require proportionate cybersecurity measures to be in place, clear records of directors' involvement, timely reporting of incidents, and transparent disclosure.

title: FINTECH-DRIVEN FINANCIAL INCLUSION: EVIDENCE FROM UZBEKISTAN'S DIGITAL PAYMENT ECOSYSTEM
summary: Financial technology (fintech) has become an important driver of financial inclusion by expanding access to digital payments, mobile banking, electronic money, and other financial services. In Uzbekistan, the rapid development of digital payment infrastructure has created new opportunities for individuals, entrepreneurs, and small businesses to participate in the formal financial system. Mobile applications, QR-code payments, online banking platforms, and electronic payment services have gradually changed the way financial transactions are conducted. This article examines the relationship between fintech development and financial inclusion in Uzbekistan, focusing on the country's digital payment ecosystem. It analyzes the opportunities created by digital financial services, their contribution to economic participation, and the challenges associated with digital literacy, cybersecurity, affordability, and unequal access to technology. The study argues that fintech can strengthen financial inclusion by reducing transaction costs, improving accessibility, and supporting small business activity. However, sustainable progress requires reliable digital infrastructure, consumer protection, financial education, and effective regulation.

title: Digital Transformation in the Workplace: Examining the Impact of Digital Tools on Employee Engagement and Productivity
summary: Abstract Digital transformation has changed the way organizations communicate, collaborate, manage performance, and engage employees. Digital tools such as communication platforms, project management systems, human resource analytics, digital learning platforms, and feedback applications have become increasingly important in contemporary workplaces, particularly with the growth of remote and hybrid work arrangements. This study examines the perceived impact of digital tools on employee engagement and productivity and identifies major benefits and challenges associated with their use. A quantitative survey-based research design was adopted, supported by insights from existing literature. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire from 110 respondents working across different sectors. Frequency and percentage analysis were used to describe respondent characteristics and responses, while one-sample right-tailed t-tests were applied to examine whether perceived productivity and engagement outcomes were significantly higher than a neutral benchmark. The findings indicate a positive perceived influence of digital tools on workplace productivity, communication, collaboration, and employee engagement. Approximately 83.33% of valid respondents perceived digital tools as effective or very effective in improving productivity, while the same proportion considered them effective or very effective in improving employee engagement. Furthermore, 93.58% of valid respondents reported that digital tools increased their productivity either significantly or to some extent. Statistical testing provided strong evidence that perceived productivity and engagement scores were significantly above the neutral level. At the same time, digital fatigue, information overload, inadequate training, privacy concerns, and excessive monitoring remain important challenges. The study concludes that digital transformation can strengthen employee engagement and organizational productivity when technology adoption is supported by appropriate training, thoughtful implementation, tool integration, employee well-being practices, and transparent management.

title: Continued Acceptance of FinTech Payment Services: An Extended UTAUT Study on University Graduates of Bangladesh
summary: Purpose: The study examines the factors influencing continued acceptance of FinTech payment services among recent university graduates in Bangladesh by extending the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology with customer trust. Research Design: A cross-sectional survey design was employed. Data were collected from 523 university graduates in Dhaka, Chattogram, and Mymensingh through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. PLS-SEM was used to assess the measurement and structural models. Results: The structural analysis revealed that performance expectancy, facilitating conditions, social influence, effort expectancy, and customer trust all showed positive and significant associations with continued acceptance of FinTech payment services. Among all, performance expectancy demonstrated the strongest positive association, with facilitating conditions and customer trust holding the subsequent positions. It indicates that graduates prioritize practical benefits, enabling resources, and confidence in service providers when deciding whether to continue using payment options. Effort expectancy and social influence also contributed meaningfully, although their effects were comparatively weaker. Originality/value: The study contributes to FinTech adoption and continuance literature by validating an extended UTAUT framework in Bangladesh and focusing on an important but underexamined population. The findings offer practical implications for policymakers, financial institutions, and FinTech providers.

title: Digital Transformation in Higher Education in the AI Era: A Systematic Review of Definitions and Emerging Trends
summary: ABSTRACT Digital transformation (DT) remains inconsistently defined in higher education, particularly as artificial intelligence (AI) introduces new institutional capabilities and responsibilities. This systematic review synthesizes 40 retrievable peer‐reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2025 to examine how DT is defined, which institutional attributes recur, and how AI is positioned within transformation. Eight attributes were identified. Strategy, leadership, and governance were the most consistently represented, followed by teaching, learning, and student experience, and technology, infrastructure, and platforms. Process redesign and data, analytics, and evidence appeared in a majority of studies, although less consistently than strategy, teaching and learning, and technology. AI was positioned through four overlapping roles: an advanced technology layer, an institution‐wide strategic capability, a teaching‐learning engine, and a governance and risk amplifier. The 2025 literature was not more AI‐saturated overall, but studies addressing AI placed substantially greater emphasis on generative AI, human readiness, and governance‐related concerns. The findings characterize DT as multidimensional socio‐technical change rather than technology adoption alone. The review proposes AI‐coupled institutional innovation, operating through dependency and consequence coupling, to explain how AI both relies on institutional conditions and generates implications that extend across pedagogical, operational, organizational, and governance domains.

title: Two Decades of FinTech and Bank Savings Research: A Bibliometric and Science Mapping Analysis (2005–2025)
summary: Purpose – This study maps twenty years of scholarship on financial technology (FinTech) and bank savings. It traces how the field grew, who shapes it, how its knowledge is structured and where its research frontier lies. Design/methodology/approach – We retrieved 603 English-language articles and reviews published between 2005 and 2025 from Scopus. Using the bibliometrix R package and its Biblioshiny interface, we combine performance analysis with science mapping: keyword co-occurrence, strategic (thematic) mapping, trend-topic analysis, co-citation analysis and bibliographic coupling. Findings – Output grew at a compound annual rate of 27.51%, and 72.3% of all documents appeared in 2020–2025. The United States (66 documents) and India (63) lead corresponding-author output, but only 3.2% of Indian papers involve international co-authorship. Financial inclusion is the dominant organising concept (231 keyword occurrences). The literature forms six thematic clusters. Banking, financial services and savings make up a basic but weakly developed theme. FinTech, mobile banking and blockchain sit on the border of the motor-theme quadrant, while central bank digital currency (CBDC) and monetary policy form an emerging theme. Research attention has shifted from internet and online banking (median years 2015–2018) to FinTech, blockchain, digital banking, financial stability and open banking (2023–2025). Savings outcomes are mostly studied indirectly, through financial inclusion. Bank-level deposit behaviour in the FinTech era remains under-examined. Originality/value – To our knowledge, this is the first science-mapping review that centres on the savings and deposit dimension of FinTech in banking rather than on FinTech or financial inclusion in general. It consolidates five research streams and proposes a structured agenda of future research questions, methods and data sources. Practical implications – The findings guide bank managers, regulators and policymakers on where evidence on digital savings products, deposit stability and inclusive savings design is robust and where it is still thin

title: Examining the Role of Corporate Governance and ESG in Curbing Energy Intensity of Indian Manufacturing Firms: An ESG Greenwashing Perspective
summary: ABSTRACT The current study centres on assessing the impact of corporate governance and ESG on the energy intensity of manufacturing firms in an Indian setting. Specifically, we examine whether the ESG mechanism aids in enhancing environmental sustainability practices or contributes to corporate greenwashing. We use a panel dataset of 325 listed Indian manufacturing firms for the period spanning from 2011 to 2023 and employ the two‐step system GMM method for empirical analysis. We exhibit that corporate governance is efficacious in minimising the firm‐level energy intensity. On the contrary, the ESG mechanism fails to reflect higher energy efficiency as it holds a positive nexus with energy intensity. Our study confirms evidence of greenwashing behaviour linked to Indian manufacturing firms through ESG. We discern that the ESG mechanism is strategically used to mislead customers and investors and reflects a mere symbolic action of sustainability reporting. Heeding such study outcomes, we provide policy suggestions for improving ESG as well as the environmental sustainability framework for Indian manufacturing firms.

title: The Mediating Role of Big Data Adoption on the Relationship between Board Governance and Audit Report Lag: Empirical Evidence from Indonesian Listed Companies
summary: Timely audited financial reporting is essential for capital market transparency, especially as companies increasingly operate in a data-intensive business environment. This study examine whether Big Data Adoption (BDA) mediates the relationship between Board Governance and Audit Report Lag (ARL) in companies in the technology, telecommunications, and healthcare sectors listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2019–2024 period. Using 294 firm-year observations, this study applies panel regression, Structural Equation Modeling (SEM), and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to test direct and indirect effects among the variables. The results indicate that BDA has a significant negative effect on ARL, suggesting that companies with higher levels of BDA tend to complete audits more quickly. BDA also significantly mediates the relationship between board size and ARL, and between board expertise and ARL. However, BDA was not found to mediate the relationship between board independence and ARL or between Board Diversity and ARL. This study extends the literature on corporate governance, audit timeliness, and digital transformation by demonstrating that board governance can reduce audit delays when supported by data-driven capabilities. These findings also provide practical implications for companies, auditors, and regulators seeking to improve audit readiness, reporting efficiency, and digital governance.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in Higher Education: A Systematic Review of Opportunities, Challenges and Emerging Trends
summary: Artificial Intelligence AI is getting more and more involved in higher education, it is reshaping teaching, learning , assessment, academic administration, research, and even how institutions decide things. In the last few years the fast rise of generative artificial intelligence GenAI, plus intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, automated assessment, recommendation systems, and AI assisted administrative tools has opened up new possibilities for universities, yet it also brings worries like academic integrity, data privacy, algorithmic bias, digital inequality, transparency, and changing professional roles. This paper actually uses a secondary-data based systematic review, looking at research and policy sources about AI and digital transformation in higher education. The review brings together outcomes from academic studies, other systematic reviews, and international policy frameworks, sort of to map out the main uses, opportunities, obstacles, and the kind of emerging trends that are starting to show up. What the literature suggests is that AI in education is not only about making content. It also includes adaptive learning, personalized tutoring, intelligent assessment, profiling and prediction, and support for institutional management. At the same time, good adoption does not just happen, it needs institutional policies, AI literacy, ethical safety nets, teacher professional development, careful responsible assessment approaches, and a human centered way of putting things into practice. A number of recent international frameworks stress human agency, ethics, AI competencies, and responsible usage, so there is a clear direction there. Overall the review shows that AI is best understood as augmentation tech with AI to help educators and learners not to flip a switch and replace the educational roles that already exist. For digital transformation a balance must exist, with technical novelty on one side and pedagogical sense together with ethical norms institutional realities and human factors, on the other. None of those should be treated as optional because leaving one out tends to break the system quickly.

title: The Controlling Effect of Corporate Governance on Human Resource Accounting and Firm Value: Evidence from Quoted Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria
summary: This study investigated how corporate governance moderates the effect of human resource accounting on market value added of quoted manufacturing firms in Nigeria. Using panel data and linear regression with PCSEs, salaries and wages (LSW) showed a significant positive effect on firm value, while training and development costs (LTDC) were positive but insignificant. Board independence (BI) and audit committee independence (ACI) revealed negative insignificant associations, reflecting a conservative influence on value creation. Diagnostic tests confirmed the suitability of the random effects model with robust corrections. The overall models were statistically significant, though with modest explanatory power (R² = 0.064). The null hypothesis was rejected, confirming corporate governance as a significant moderator. The study underscores the importance of human resource accounting and governance structures in enhancing firm value and provides insights for managers, policymakers, and researchers.

title: Greenwashing or Sustainability Misalignment? Analysing Organisational, Workplace and Real Estate Strategies Through an Iceberg Lens
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental sustainability and the broader Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) agenda have become prominently proclaimed organisational priorities, yet their integration into core decision‐making remains uneven. While greenwashing research has largely focused on communication and disclosure, it has paid less attention to the internal strategic dynamics that underpin sustainability outcomes. This paper examines how environmental sustainability and ESG shape organisational decision‐making in workplace and corporate real estate (CRE) strategies. Drawing on organisational culture and institutional theory, the study adopts an iceberg perspective, conceptualising sustainability as a visible commitment underpinned by less visible strategic, cultural and institutional dynamics. Using a mixed‐methods design, the study combines quantitative analysis of two waves of large‐scale survey data from senior CRE professionals with qualitative insights from semistructured interviews with employees, senior executives and CRE managers. The findings show that sustainability and ESG considerations may be unevenly associated with workplace and CRE strategies. It revealed that sustainability may be largely peripheral to future strategic decision‐making, with stronger links to workplace adjustments than to fundamental CRE portfolio decisions. Qualitative evidence further shows that economic, operational and social priorities dominate stakeholder workplace considerations, while organisations weakly prioritise environmental sustainability in routines. The study shows that sustainability may be rhetorically prominent yet strategically peripheral, reframing sustainability misalignment as an underlying strategic integration challenge that spans business, organisational strategy and sustainability research, and offering insights for organisations seeking to align ESG commitments more effectively with asset‐intensive strategies.

title: Ai & Fintech-Driven Transformation of the Inidian Financial Management System: An Empirical Study of Digital Payments, Blockchain Technology, & Cryptocurrency
summary: Abstract The rapid advancement of Financial Technology (FinTech) has significantly transformed the structure and functioning of the Indian financial system. The growth of digital payment platforms, mobile banking, artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing and data-driven financial services has changed the way individuals and businesses access and use financial services. In India, digital payments have emerged as an important component of financial transformation, while Artificial Intelligence is increasingly being used for fraud detection, credit assessment, customer service, risk management and personalised financial services.This study examines the role of FinTech in transforming the Indian financial system, with particular emphasis on digital payments and Artificial Intelligence. The study proposes an analytical framework linking FinTech adoption, digital payment usage, AI-enabled financial services, consumer trust, cybersecurity and financial inclusion. A structured questionnaire can be used to collect primary data from users of digital financial services. The proposed study may employ descriptive statistics, correlation and regression analysis to examine relationships among the major variables. The paper also discusses opportunities and challenges associated with technology-driven financial transformation, including cybersecurity risks, digital fraud, data privacy, technological barriers and the digital divide.

title: Reimagining Sustainable Natural Resource Governance through the Paradigm of Maqāṣid Al-Sharī‘ah and Ecological Justice
summary: The exploitation of natural resources and environmental degradation call for sustainable governance grounded in ethical and normative values. This study aims to identify Islamic principles in responding to contemporary environmental governance challenges and their relevance to sustainable natural resource management. This study employs a qualitative-descriptive approach through an integrative literature review of 25 scientific publications, primarily from 2021–2026, using content analysis and thematic synthesis. The results indicate that there are eight sustainable governance strategies closely linked to Islamic values within the framework of maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah, including public interest-based planning, regulation, participation, accountability, and law enforcement which reflect the principles of justice (‘adl) and stewardship (amānah),pollution monitoring, ecosystem restoration, and sustainability evaluation grounded in the principles of balance (mīzān) and ecological stewardship (khilāfah). The contribution of this research is that it offers an integrative framework for environmental governance that is equitable, sustainable, and oriented toward the well-being of future generations.

title: FOREIGN EXPERIENCE OF HIGHER EDUCATION FUNDING AND ITS APPLICABILITY IN UZBEKISTAN: TOWARDS A HYBRID MODEL WITH MATCHING ESTIMATE AND ACCOUNTING RULES
summary: Uzbekistan is moving its state universities from line-item budget estimates to per-student formula funding. This thesis asks which elements of foreign funding models can be transferred and what they require from budget estimates, accounting and reporting. Funding mechanisms in Finland, Denmark, the Netherlands, England, the United States, the Russian Federation and Kazakhstan are compared by funding unit, planning document and reporting format. OECD cost-structure benchmarks are set against the tuition-fee expenditure of a large Uzbek university, and five model types are scored against six criteria. Formula funding fits current legislation best (24 points), while a hybrid model (22 points) offers stronger performance incentives at similar financial stability. A hybrid design with base, performance and targeted components is proposed, together with a single financial plan covering all sources and auditable performance indicators.

title: CEO power and stock price crash risk: moderating effect of environmental practices
summary: Abstract This paper investigates the influence of CEO power on corporate stock price crash risk in developed market context, and further examines the moderating impact of corporate environmental practices. Two environmental practices are examined: greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and Sustainable Development Goal 13 (SDG-13 supporting climate action). Analysing data from publicly listed firms in the G7 nations from 2006 to 2021, empirical results show that firms led by more powerful CEOs are generally exposed to lower crash risks. Additionally, results show that companies implementing stronger environmentally friendly practices, particularly, supporting climate actions - SDG-13, see a further reduced crash risk. This pattern is especially evident in non-crisis period, non-financial firms, and firms with high environmental and social (ES) scores, i.e., Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) performance. The findings are validated by various robustness tests using alternative estimation models, alternative measures, and additional tests. Our findings provide practical implications for firms, investors, regulators, and policymakers.

title: Operational strategies for managing purchase decisions in festival shopping: Analyzing the role of fear of missing out (FOMO) in the digital transformation era
summary: Purpose: For most consumers who experience fear of missing out, regret related to falling behind trends outweighs regret related to financial costs. In fact, the intensity of the attraction created through fear of missing out is positively correlated with impulse buying, which potentially reduces self-control during shopping activities. Hence, fear of missing out is considered a psychological disorder that affects the mental health of the individual. Therefore, this study aims to explain the reactive-behavioral outcomes (e.g., impulsive buying decisions) by emphasizing the perceptual drivers of the 'Fear Of Missing Out' (FOMO) phenomenon within the context of festival shopping opportunities in the digital transformation era.Methodology: This study is a basic-applied research based on its purpose and a mixed research based on its research strategy. The qualitative strategy used in the first stage of the research is grounded theory and the quantitative strategies used in this survey-correlational research. The qualitative participants included marketing and sales consultants as well as professors of business, marketing, and e-commerce, 10 of whom were selected as participants through non-probability judgmental sampling. The statistical population of the quantitative part of the study is people who visited various festivals and made various purchases.The sampling method in the quantitative section was random, and the sample size was determined to be 221 participants based on relationship of Cohen. To prevent sample attrition, about 240 questionnaires were distributed in this study and 229 questionnaires were returned to the researcher.Findings: The results showed that perceptual drivers (positive customer perception of the brand, deceptive advertising, customer experience, and customer emotional intelligence) lead to strengthening the fear of missing out on festival shopping opportunities. Also, the pivotal phenomenon (fear of missing out on festival shopping opportunities), individual-marketing factors, and technological factors lead to strengthening customer acumen (smart and responsible shopping, strengthening the buyer's financial knowledge and awareness, and managing market rumors). Finally, it was determined that customer intelligence (smart and responsible shopping, strengthening the buyer's financial knowledge and awareness, and managing market rumors) leads to a reduction in undesirable behavioral-reactive outcomes and a strengthening of desirable behavioral-reactive outcomes.Originality/Value: According to the results obtained from the implementation of the qualitative and quantitative parts of the research, the variables 1) deceptive advertising, 2) customer emotional intelligence, 3) customer respect for the brand, 4) buyer confusion, 5) brand uniqueness, 6) brand community, 7) brand love, 8) brand attachment, 9) customer thirst for shopping, 10) market rumor management, 11) digital age, 12) negative internal emotions, 13) customer mental anxiety, 14) interaction-communication problems, and 15) customer resentment, 16) brand responsibility are considered new research findings.

title: The assessment of the presentations at the Fourth International Conference on Real Estate Development and Management (ICREDM 2025)
summary: The climate crisis, financial fluctuations, and urbanization pressures have transformed the real estate sector from a purely economic activity into a multi-layered policy domain. This study evaluates the thematic content and sectoral reflections of the Fourth International Conference on Real Estate Development and Management (ICREDM 2025), held in Ankara on February 3–5, 2025. Structured around the main theme “Residential and Commercial Real Estate Markets Under Climate Crisis and Financial Risk and Their Future,” the conference brought together more than 130 academics, experts and other stakeholders from over 20 countries and comprehensively addressed multidisciplinary topics. Through qualitative analysis, the study examines more than 100 papers presented at the conference, as well as its 14 thematic sessions, 3 panel sessions, and 1 roundtable meeting. The roundtable meeting produced strategic outcomes on the discipline's institutionalization, education reforms, and the definition of sectoral competencies. The conference covered eight topics: the impacts of disaster risk and the climate crisis on real estate markets; the integration of artificial intelligence and digital technologies into the sector; the transformation of valuation processes; the restructuring of housing security and social housing policies; and green finance and the circular economy. ICREDM 2025 stands out not merely as an academic event but also as a platform for redefining the real estate development and management discipline in line with the principles of social responsibility, sustainability, and strategic governance. The conference's output contributes to developing a collective vision for the discipline's future while also strengthening the production of practice-oriented knowledge.

title: Municipal Utility Billing, Debt Collection and Public Accountability in Latvia: An Independent Documentary and Legal Assessment (2023–2026)
summary: This independent documentary and legal research report examines questions of municipal utility billing accuracy, financial accountability, digital data migration, and outsourced debt recovery in Latvia, with particular reference to SIA “Ķekavas nami”, the Bill.me platform, and SIA “PAUS KONSULTS”. The research draws on municipal committee minutes, publicly available financial statements, internal governance documents, procurement-related information, regulatory register screenshots, and an accompanying documentary appendix. Particular attention is given to the Ķekava Municipality Finance Committee meeting of 24 April 2025, during which a proposal was supported to advance an audit addressing revenue accounting, water-meter readings, billing data transfers, internal controls, and data migration involving Bill.me. The report also examines the relationship between a reported debt-recovery contract dated 31 March 2025 and a PTAC public-register entry for PAUS KONSULTS dated 8 May 2025. The difference between these dates is identified as a matter requiring historical licensing verification, not as evidence of unlawful conduct. The legal discussion addresses Latvian debt-recovery regulation, consumer protection, data accuracy, GDPR principles, public procurement, municipal governance, financial reporting, and evidentiary standards. Research limitations: This publication does not constitute a forensic audit, judicial determination, or finding of fraud, corruption, unlawful debt recovery, or individual liability. It distinguishes documented facts from unresolved questions and identifies records necessary for further verification. Public-interest purpose: To support transparent, evidence-based examination of billing controls, consumer safeguards, regulatory accountability, and the governance of municipally owned service providers in Latvia. title: Investigating the Impact of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation on Organizational Decision-Making, Human Resource Management, and Employee Productivity in the Electrical Power Industry
summary: Background: Electrical power organizations are adopting artificial intelligence (AI), digital twins, advanced analytics, and workflow automation while facing aging infrastructure, changing load patterns, scarce specialist labor, and strict reliability obligations. Objective: This article investigates how AI-enabled digital transformation relates to organizational decision-making, human resource management (HRM), and employee productivity in electricity generation, transmission, distribution, and utility support functions. Methods: An integrative, structured narrative review of identifiable 2024-2026 peer-reviewed studies and reports from recognized research and standards organizations was undertaken. A cross-domain evidence matrix aligned operational use cases with organizational mechanisms, workforce outcomes, and assurance requirements. No primary interviews, experiments, or utility microdata were collected; thus no causal effect estimates are claimed. Results: The evidence supports a contingent model in which improved data availability and predictive capability can accelerate routine decisions, prioritize asset work, and support forecasting, whereas gains in human productivity depend on role redesign, training, trust, interoperability, and oversight. Benefits differ materially between office-based knowledge work and physically performed grid tasks. Algorithmic HRM creates opportunities for workforce planning and skill development but can also magnify bias, surveillance, opacity, and stress. Conclusion: Digital transformation is better understood as a jointly technical and organizational capability than as software deployment. A staged, human-accountable governance architecture and a multidimensional evaluation scorecard are proposed for future empirical testing.

title: Prioritizing and selecting the G-resilient suppliers in the natural stone industry using a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making approach: BWM-TRUST
summary: Purpose: In today's turbulent and uncertain environment, organizations are compelled to revise traditional supply chain approaches and adopt strategies that simultaneously address environmental sustainability and resilience to disruptions. Accordingly, this study aims to develop a decision-making framework for evaluating and selecting green-resilient suppliers in the natural stone industry—suppliers that demonstrate both strong environmental performance and the ability to respond quickly and effectively to disruptions. Methodology: This research employs a hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) framework that integrates the Best-Worst Method (BWM) to determine the weights of evaluation criteria with the mulTi-noRmalization mUltiDistance aSsessmenT (TRUST) technique to rank suppliers as alternatives. The evaluation criteria, categorized into "green" and "resilience" dimensions, were identified through a comprehensive literature review and expert input. These criteria include: waste generation, employee training, possession of eco-friendly certifications, pollution control initiatives, responsiveness, coordination, agility, information sharing, and efficient resource utilization. Data related to five real suppliers in the natural stone industry were collected through expert surveys and fed into the proposed evaluation model. Findings: The results revealed that "efficient resource utilization" holds the highest weight among the green and resilience criteria. Furthermore, based on the TRUST-based ranking, supplier A2 was identified as the top-performing green-resilient supplier. Originality/Value: The proposed model offers a practical, structured tool to help supply chain managers enhance sustainability and resilience amid growing environmental and operational disruptions.

title: The Impact of Business Environmental Changes on the Adoption of a Strategic Pivot: A Case Study of Zar Industrial Group
summary: Objective: This study aimed to examine the impact of business environmental changes on strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group and develop a conceptual model of this process. Methods and Materials: This applied qualitative study used a grounded theory design. The study population consisted of Zar Industrial Group managers and university professors with expertise in strategic management and organizational change. Participants were selected purposively based on their knowledge and professional experience. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with managers of the holding company and its food-industry subsidiaries, together with academic experts. Interviews continued until theoretical saturation, resulting in a final sample of 12 participants. Interview transcripts were systematically coded, compared, and categorized to identify the principal dimensions and mechanisms associated with strategic pivot adoption. Findings: The analysis produced seven main categories and 41 related concepts. The categories included macro-environmental changes and external pressures; risk, uncertainty, and financial pressure; supply-chain and operational disruptions; market-oriented and commercial responses; structural and business-model redesign; innovation, technology, and digital transformation; and human capital, organizational learning, and institutionalization of the strategic pivot. Environmental turbulence generated financial, operational, and market pressures that stimulated coordinated strategic responses. These responses involved market reorientation, business-model redesign, technological innovation, digital transformation, and capability development. Human capital and organizational learning played a central role in sustaining and institutionalizing the strategic pivot. Conclusion: Strategic pivot adoption in Zar Industrial Group represents a multidimensional organizational response to environmental uncertainty rather than an isolated managerial decision. Successful pivots require alignment among market responses, structural transformation, technological innovation, operational resilience, and organizational learning. The proposed conceptual model can help managers recognize environmental signals, coordinate adaptive actions, and strengthen organizational resilience and long-term competitiveness.

title: Climate Change and Its Impact on Global Politics
summary: Abstract: Climate is the average weather of an area. Climate refers to the long- term pattern of weather conditions in a particular place or region, usually measured over a period of thirty years or more. It includes factors such as temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind, and atmospheric pressure. Climate change has emerged as one of the most significant challenges to contemporary global politics. Climate change refers to long-term changes in the Earth’s temperature, rainfall, wind patterns, and other climatic conditions. Today, the major cause of rapid climate change is the increase in greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide largely due to human activities. Its impacts extend beyond environmental concerns, influencing international relations, economic security, and global governance. Rising temperatures, extreme weather events, sea-level rise, and increasing pressure on natural resources have created new challenges for states and international institutions. Climate change has also intensified debates between developed and developing countries concerning historical responsibility, climate finance, technology transfer and equitable burden-sharing. International agreements such as the Paris Agreement demonstrate the importance of multilateral cooperation, while differences in national interests often complicate collective action. Furthermore, climate related displacement and competition over scarce resources may contribute to social and political instability in vulnerable regions. This paper examines the relationship between climate change and global politics, focusing on its influence on international cooperation, geopolitical relations, security, and sustainable development. It argues that addressing climate change requires stronger multilateral institutions, equitable international cooperation, and policies that integrate environmental sustainability with global peace and development.

title: Perceived green-shipping knowledge and competency demands among Chinese enterprise respondents: an exploratory network analysis
summary: Workforce-needs surveys can conflate broad endorsement, uniform answering and specific relations among knowledge domains. We applied a measurement-aware diagnostic analysis to perceived green-shipping knowledge and competency demands. In a non-probability online survey, 93 Chinese enterprise respondents rated seven study-specific knowledge domains and selected six generic competencies; no invitation denominator was retained. Ratings were ceiling-concentrated (80.6–91.4% rated 4 or 5), and 41 respondents used one rating across all seven domains. A regularised network retained 15 of 21 positive edges, but centrality was unstable (CS = 0.10 for strength; CS = 0.20 for expected influence). We compared the observed edges with two post hoc simulation benchmarks, one reproducing a general importance factor and the other fixing the composition and margins of the 41 uniform-response records, using 20,000 datasets per benchmark under fixed-penalty and penalty-reselected estimation. Energy efficiency–clean fuels alone met the four-condition sensitivity criterion (q = 0.00105–0.00367); digitalisation–ESG was model-selection sensitive. No knowledge–competency correlation survived multiplicity correction. Thus, the survey does not establish a stable population network or observed task coupling. It identifies one association that persists under the specified sensitivity analyses and a diagnostic approach for separating survey-wide endorsement from candidate pair-specific workforce needs.

title: Roadmap of MSME Growth Strategies in India
summary: Abstract Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises are central to India’s employment generation, entrepreneurship, industrial supply chains and local economic development. title: Transformasi digital pengelolaan penjualan dan keuangan pada Umkm Pray Florist
summary: ABSTRACT Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) continue to face challenges in managing sales and financial activities, particularly due to manual record-keeping processes. Pray Florist, an MSME operating in the fresh flower business, still relied on handwritten notes and simple spreadsheets for transaction recording, resulting in difficulties in report generation and business decision-making. This community service program aimed to support the digital transformation of Pray Florist through the implementation of a web-based smart dashboard. The program employed a Participatory Research approach consisting of planning, design, development, training and mentoring, and evaluation stages. The results showed that the developed system was able to assist the partner in recording transactions, generating sales and financial reports, and presenting business information through a visual dashboard. Evaluation results indicated that the dashboard helped users better understand business conditions, supported data-driven decision-making, assisted promotional strategies, and improved flower inventory planning. Although several features still require further improvement and more intensive utilization, the implemented system has contributed to improving operational efficiency and supporting the digital transformation of Pray Florist. title: Enabling artificial intelligence in entrepreneurship: Implications for startup creation in higher education
summary: The digital transformation has reshaped entrepreneurship, with the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful enabler of innovation and startup creation. However, higher education institutions face challenges integrating AI into entrepreneurship education curriculum, limiting students’ ability to fully harness its potential. This study aimed to determine and explore entrepreneurship students’ challenges in using AI for startup development, assess the competencies they gain in innovating business ideas, and analyze how these challenges affect competencies using structural equation modeling (SEM). Employing an convergent mixed-method design, the study surveyed 114 third- and fourth-year BS Entrepreneurship students and conducted interviews to faculty and business plan implementers. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and SEM, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis for triangulation. Findings revealed that students face significant challenges in opportunity identification, decision-making, performance execution, education and learning, and research application. The key barriers highlight was market understanding, lack of AI literacy, limited mentorship, and insufficient curriculum integration. Despite these, students reported gaining competencies in opportunity recognition, customer targeting, data-informed decision-making, and entrepreneurial communication using AI tools. However, critical thinking, problem-solving, and prototyping skills remained underdeveloped. SEM results indicated that challenges in education, opportunity identification, and decision-making significantly constrained entrepreneurial competencies. The study implies the need for higher education to reform curricula by embedding AI-focused modules, case-based projects, mentorship opportunities, and innovation hubs. Strengthening AI-driven entrepreneurship education will equip students with the competencies required for sustainable startup creation in the digital economy.

title: AN INTEGRATED MODEL OF THE ECONOMIC TRANSFORMATION OF SMART URBAN SPACE: FINANCIAL, ECONOMIC, AND INSTITUTIONAL FOUNDATIONS
summary: The transformation of smart urban spaces can enhance the quality of life by improving municipal services and resource efficiency. However, it requires addressing cybersecurity, digital inequality, investment needs, and opportunities for innovation. This article presents a comprehensive analysis of the key components of an integrated approach to implementing the smart space concept in Ukraine. Particular attention is paid to the mechanisms for establishing strategic priorities that ensure the effectiveness of transformative economic changes in urban environments. The aim of the study is to assess the statistical relationships between the digital, socio-economic, financial, and security characteristics of territories and their Gross Regional Product (GRP) per capita, and to build on this basis a financial model for the economic transformation of the smart urban space. The research employs regression analysis to evaluate factors of economic performance, econometric diagnostics to verify model adequacy, and an indexing method to determine the Security Index. The constructed regression model serves as the quantitative foundation for the financial transformation model, enabling an assessment of the links between employment, the digital economy, per capita capital investment, digital public services, and security, on the one hand, and GRP per capita, on the other. Statistically significant relation-ships with per capita GRP were found for employment (0.88), the digital economy (-0.34), per capita capital investment (0.56), digital public services (0.43), and the Security Index (-0.43). The obtained results define the quantitative parameters of a financial model for the economic transformation of smart urban space. Here, the financial model is understood as an econometric model of GRP per capita that serves as a quantitative basis for a financial-economic frame-work; the analysis is conducted at the regional level. The article outlines the key principles of an integrated approach to implementing the smart space concept in Ukraine. An integrated model has been developed within the framework of the concept of intellectualizing urban space in Ukraine. Particular attention is paid to mechanisms for analysing these components and their practical application. Examples of existing methodologies that enable the effective implementation of analysis mechanisms, ensuring a comprehensive and systemic approach to smart city development, were analysed. The research findings contribute to refining tools for strategic planning and the implementation of transformative initiatives aimed at rebuilding smart space.

title: Enabling artificial intelligence in entrepreneurship: Implications for startup creation in higher education
summary: The digital transformation has reshaped entrepreneurship, with the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful enabler of innovation and startup creation. However, higher education institutions face challenges integrating AI into entrepreneurship education curriculum, limiting students’ ability to fully harness its potential. This study aimed to determine and explore entrepreneurship students’ challenges in using AI for startup development, assess the competencies they gain in innovating business ideas, and analyze how these challenges affect competencies using structural equation modeling (SEM). Employing an convergent mixed-method design, the study surveyed 114 third- and fourth-year BS Entrepreneurship students and conducted interviews to faculty and business plan implementers. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and SEM, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis for triangulation. Findings revealed that students face significant challenges in opportunity identification, decision-making, performance execution, education and learning, and research application. The key barriers highlight was market understanding, lack of AI literacy, limited mentorship, and insufficient curriculum integration. Despite these, students reported gaining competencies in opportunity recognition, customer targeting, data-informed decision-making, and entrepreneurial communication using AI tools. However, critical thinking, problem-solving, and prototyping skills remained underdeveloped. SEM results indicated that challenges in education, opportunity identification, and decision-making significantly constrained entrepreneurial competencies. The study implies the need for higher education to reform curricula by embedding AI-focused modules, case-based projects, mentorship opportunities, and innovation hubs. Strengthening AI-driven entrepreneurship education will equip students with the competencies required for sustainable startup creation in the digital economy.

title: Pengaruh Intensitas Modal, Leverage, dan CSR terhadap Agresivitas Pajak Perusahaan Manufaktur di BEI
summary: This study examines the effect of capital intensity, leverage, and corporate social responsibility (CSR) on the tax aggressiveness of manufacturing firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). The study is motivated by the declining tax contribution of the manufacturing sector and by inconsistent findings in prior research. Tax aggressiveness is proxied by the cash effective tax rate (CETR), where a lower CETR indicates more aggressive tax behaviour. Using purposive sampling, the study analyses 93 firms, yielding 465 firm-year observations over the 2019–2024 period. The data are analysed using panel data regression; the Chow and Hausman tests indicate that the fixed effect model (FEM) is the most appropriate estimator. The results show that capital intensity and CSR have no significant effect on CETR; therefore, neither variable is associated with tax aggressiveness. Leverage has a significant negative effect on CETR (β = −0.174; p = 0.018), indicating that higher leverage is associated with a lower cash effective tax rate and thus with higher tax aggressiveness. This finding contradicts the hypothesised negative relationship. The deductibility of interest expense offers a plausible theoretical explanation, although this mechanism is not tested directly in the model. Practically, the results suggest that tax authorities should consider debt-financing structures in risk-based tax supervision and that investors should interpret the low effective tax rates of highly leveraged firms with caution. Future research is encouraged to test the interest tax-shield mechanism directly and to employ alternative proxies of tax aggressiveness.

title: A Study on The Evolving Financial Landscape, Risk Dynamics and Institutional Integration of Cryptocurrency in India
summary: Abstract The rapid development of cryptocurrency and blockchain technology has significantly influenced the global financial landscape, creating new opportunities for digital financial innovation while introducing various financial, technological, and regulatory challenges. This study examines the evolving financial landscape of cryptocurrency in India, with particular emphasis on risk dynamics and institutional integration. It explores the development of Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs), the major risks associated with cryptocurrency, and the regulatory mechanisms introduced by the Government of India and financial authorities. The study focuses on market volatility, cybersecurity threats, consumer protection, money laundering, financial stability, taxation, and Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing (AML/CFT) compliance. It also examines the growing relationship between cryptocurrency-related activities, financial institutions, fintech organisations, and India's broader digital-finance ecosystem. The research adopts a secondary and descriptive analytical approach based on publications from the Reserve Bank of India, the Income Tax Department, the Financial Intelligence Unit–India, the Bank for International Settlements, and other credible sources. The study highlights the importance of balancing technological innovation with effective regulation, risk management, and consumer protection. It concludes that a transparent and well-structured regulatory framework is essential for addressing cryptocurrency-related risks and supporting the responsible development of India's digital financial ecosystem.

title: Design and Evaluation of an Interactive Power BI-Based Financial Mis Dashboard
summary: Managing financial information from multiple sales channels requires the analysis of revenue, taxes, refunds, cancellations, cost of goods sold, and profit margins. When these metrics are maintained across different sources, preparing consolidated reports and comparing financial performance can become time-consuming. This paper presents an interactive financial Management Information System (MIS) dashboard developed using Microsoft Power BI to support multichannel financial reporting and profitability analysis. The dashboard provides monthly profit-and-loss summaries, channel-wise comparisons, date-based filtering, and dynamic visualizations that allow users to examine selected financial measures. Because real financial records are confidential, the study also presents a validation framework that uses independently generated synthetic data to verify calculation accuracy, aggregation consistency, and filter behavior without disclosing sensitive business information. The work demonstrates how interactive business intelligence can support consistent and flexible financial reporting for multichannel businesses.

title: How Environmental, Social, and Governance Mediates the Impact of FinTech Investments on Bank Performance in Gulf Countries
summary: This study examines the FinTech factors affecting bank performance in Gulf countries. The study followed a causal research design employing data from 2010 to 2023. The study unit of analysis is twelve banks in Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. The study also uses PLS-SEM because of its advantage in examining mediating pathways that might be obscured in simpler regression analyses. According to the study’s findings, FinTech factors such as mobile banking applications (MBA) and GDP per capita variables have a negative, statistically significant effect on bank performance. On the other hand, GDP per capita has not statistically positively affected both ROA and ROE of bank performance. Moreover, both MBA and GDP per capita directly enhance environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance. The ESG does affect ROE. Besides, ESG plays a mediating role by strengthening the relationship between MBA, GDP per capita, and ROE, as it enhances banks ESG performance. The current study fills a gap in the body of literature since it considers previously overlooked factors that affect bank performance, i.e., FinTech variables and the mediating role of ESG on their effects on bank performance. The resulting policy implication is that banks in Gulf countries benefit most from investing in FinTech innovation since they can enhance operational efficiency and support sustainability efforts by driving better ESG performance, ultimately fostering long term stability and growth in the banking sector.

title: Corporate Governance, Board Oversight, and Firm Value: Evidence from Listed Insurance Companies in Nigeria
summary: Effective board oversight is essential for corporate governance, accountability, and the sustainable value of firms. This study examines how board oversight functions relate to firm value and how this relationship has evolved among listed insurance companies in Nigeria. An ex post facto research design was employed, utilising secondary data from the annual reports and financial statements of 21 listed insurance companies from 2012 to 2021, resulting in 210 firm-year observations. Board oversight was assessed through audit committee, risk management, and remuneration governance functions, while firm value was measured using Market-to-Net Book Value (MNBV) and Tobin’s Q. Descriptive statistics, trend analysis, diagnostic tests, and regression analysis were conducted. The results show that firm value changed considerably throughout the period examined. Audit committee and remuneration governance functions demonstrated positive and statistically significant relationships with firm value, whereas risk management functions exhibited a negative and statistically significant relationship. These results suggest that strengthening board oversight mechanisms may improve, particularly risk management practices, to improve governance effectiveness and support sustainable firm value in Nigeria’s insurance industry.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Accounting: An Empirical Study on Its Impact on Financial Reporting Quality and Managerial Decision - Making in Thrissur District, Kerala
summary: Abstract Applications of artificial intelligence include machine learning, document processing, anomaly detection, predictive analytics, and generative AI, which have brought about a change in the field of accounting. The present study aims to examine the impact of artificial intelligence on three aspects of accounting namely accounting efficiency, financial reporting quality and the effectiveness of managerial decision making. Primary data will be collected from 200 respondents in Thrissur District, Kerala, using structured questionnaires. The respondents to this study are those who are working in the areas of accounting and finance, auditing, academia, and other people having knowledge of accounting or financial information systems. The responses shall be measured using a five-point Likert scale. Analysis will entail the use of descriptive statistics, reliability test, correlation and regression analysis depending on data characteristics and assumptions. Implementation challenges in this case include data quality, cybersecurity, privacy issues, employee capability and human supervision.

title: Digital transformation is associated with lower ecological footprint across developed and developing economies
summary: The rapid expansion of the digital economy is transforming global production and consumption systems, yet its environmental implications remain insufficiently understood. This study examines the relationship between the Digital Economy Index (DEI) and ecological footprint (EF) across 77 developed and developing countries from 2001 to 2020. An integrated empirical framework combining fixed-effects and System GMM estimation with machine learning techniques, Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), is employed to provide complementary econometric and predictive evidence. Econometric results show that digitalization significantly reduces EF on average, with stronger environmental benefits observed in developed economies. Moderation analysis reveals that industrialization and trade openness weaken these environmental benefits, whereas artificial intelligence, ICT development, and renewable energy transitions strengthen them. The transmission-channel analysis further suggests that environmental technological innovation and changes in the energy structure may represent potential pathways linking digitalization to environmental outcomes. The machine learning analysis provides complementary predictive evidence and identifies a nonlinear pattern in the DEI–EF relationship, potentially exhibiting an inverted U-shape in which ecological pressure increases at earlier stages of digitalization but declines at more advanced stages. RF and SVM achieve predictive accuracies of 94% and 80%, respectively. Overall, the findings indicate that digitalization is not inherently green and that its environmental benefits depend on the stage of digital development and broader structural and technological conditions, highlighting the importance of clean energy integration and sustainable digital transformation.

title: THE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE REVOLUTION IN FINANCE: FROM ALGORITHMS TO STRATEGIC SOLUTIONS
summary: A rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is transforming the financial sector, changing approaches to automating operations, analyzing data bulk, forecasting, risk management, customer service, and making management decisions. The relevance of the study is due to the need to transition from the fragmented and predominantly operational use of algorithmic tools to their systemic integration into strategic management in finance. The purpose of the study is to systematize the areas of application of AI in the financial sector and substantiate the conceptual model of the transition from the operational use of algorithmic tools to the strategic level of management. To achieve the set goal, systemic, historical-logical, comparative, and classification methods were used. The main results of the study are the identification of four stages of the evolution of AI applications in finance: algorithmic-rule, machine learning, deep learning, and generative-strategic. The key areas of AI use are systematized by the level of managerial influence - from the automation of routine operations and support of individual business processes to forecasting, risk management, personalization of financial services, and the formation of strategic management decisions. The technological, regulatory, reputational, ethical, and systemic risks associated with scaling AI in the financial sector are summarized. A five-level maturity model of AI application is proposed, which involves a sequential transition from experimental, operational, and integrated levels to the level of managerial transformation and strategic use of technologies.It is concluded that the strategic value of AI is determined not by the number of implemented technological solutions, but by the degree of their integration into the corporate governance system, the quality and availability of data, the effectiveness of model management, personnel competencies, the explainability of algorithmic solutions, compliance with regulatory requirements, and the effectiveness of risk control. The strategic integration of AI creates the prerequisites for increasing the adaptability, competitiveness, and sustainability of the financial sector.

title: BARRIERS TO IMPLEMENTING AGILE MANAGEMENT IN TAX AUTHORITIES AND WAYS TO OVERCOME THEM
summary: Abstract. This scientific article examines the major organizational, institutional, technological, and human factors that hinder the implementation of Agile management in tax authorities and analyzes possible approaches to overcoming these barriers. In the context of accelerating digital transformation and public sector modernization, tax authorities are increasingly required to develop flexible, responsive, transparent, and citizen-oriented management systems. From this perspective, Agile management represents a promising managerial approach that can improve decision-making speed, strengthen cooperation among employees and departments, enhance the quality of public services, and increase the ability of tax authorities to respond effectively to changing economic, technological, and regulatory conditions. The article focuses particular attention on bureaucratic organizational structures, resistance to organizational change, limited employee autonomy, insufficient digital competencies, inadequate technological infrastructure, weak cross-functional cooperation, and the lack of an Agile-oriented organizational culture. Furthermore, practical measures for overcoming these barriers are proposed, including strong managerial support, continuous professional development, gradual implementation of Agile principles, improvement of digital infrastructure, development of cross-functional teams, and enhancement of internal communication mechanisms. The study concludes that the systematic adaptation of Agile management principles to tax administration can contribute to greater organizational efficiency, improved service quality, increased employee engagement, and enhanced institutional flexibility. The findings provide a theoretical and practical basis for modernizing tax administration through Agile-oriented management approaches. title: Effect of Financial Management Practices on Construction Project Implementation: A Case of Amahoro Stadium in Gasabo District, Rwanda
summary: The study examined the effect of financial management practices on implementation of Amahoro Stadium Project in Gasabo District, Rwanda. The study guided by two specific objectives: to assess the effect of financial planning on implementation of Amahoro Stadium Project, to examine the effect of financial control on implementation of Amahoro Stadium Project. The study anchored on Resource-Based View Theory. A descriptive and correlational research design were applied using quantitative and qualitative approaches. The target population comprised 324 populations. The sample size was 179 respondents selected using Slovin’s formula, while stratified and simple random sampling techniques guided participant selection. Questionnaires, interviews, and documentary review served as data collection instruments, and SPSS version 29 used to analyze quantitative data through descriptive statistics, correlation, and multiple regression. Qualitative data was analyzed thematically to support interpretation of statistical findings and strengthen conclusions on how financial management practices affect project implementation. The findings showed that Financial Planning had a positive and significant effect on project implementation (β = 0.194, t = 2.896, p = 0.004); Financial Control had a positive and significant effect on project implementation (β = 0.306, t = 5.016, p = 0.000). The study concluded that financial management practices significantly contributed to project implementation in Amahoro Stadium Project. It recommended that responsible institutions should strengthen budget forecasting, cost estimation and cash scheduling before each implementation phase while also strengthening the other significant practices identified by the study. Keywords: Project implementation, financial reporting, financial accountability, financial control, financial planning, and Financial management practices.

title: Digital Entrepreneurship and Territorial Bricolage: The Mechanisms Underlying the Construction of a Smart Territory in Dakhla-Oued Eddahab
summary: In peripheral territories with still limited digital resources, the emergence of innovative entrepreneurial practices raises questions about the concrete mechanisms through which digital technology contributes to building a smart territory. This is the case of the Dakhla-Oued Eddahab region, engaged in a digital transformation dynamic driven by national strategies and the Morocco Digital 2030 vision, yet where entrepreneurs must navigate significant territorial constraints. This research aims to understand how entrepreneurs mobilize territorial bricolage to turn these constraints into levers for building a smart territory in Dakhla-Oued Eddahab. The study adopts an interpretivist qualitative stance based on a single case study. Twenty semi-structured interviews were conducted with stakeholders of the regional ecosystem and analyzed through a reflexive thematic analysis assisted by Nvivo12, following an abductive approach. The findings show that the contribution of digital entrepreneurship to smart territory construction rests on the interaction between digital infrastructure, territorial governance, entrepreneurial ecosystem dynamics, and entrepreneurs' adaptive capabilities. They further reveal an emerging mechanism, territorial digital entrepreneurial bricolage, through which entrepreneurs creatively mobilize locally available resources to overcome structural constraints. This mechanism enriches the theoretical model and opens avenues for other comparable peripheral territories.
