title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Financial Performance: The Mediating Role of Employee Engagement and the Moderating Role of Job Autonomy in Malaysian Manufacturing Firms
summary: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) has historically been treated as a discretionary activity outside the realm of strategic management. However, over time CSR has gained traction as a necessary addition to any organisation with positive impact on the firm’s bottom line. Despite this progress, how CSR affects financial performance is not well understood, especially in an emerging- market manufacturing setting. This study investigates CSR’s impact on financial performance for Malaysian manufacturing firms while testing employee engagement as a mediating variable and job autonomy as a moderating condition. Five hypotheses were formulated on the basis of Stakeholder Theory, Social Exchange Theory, and Self-Determination Theory; direct effects of CSR on employee engagement and financial performance, the indirect effect of employee engagement on financial performance, mediation of employee engagement, and moderation of job autonomy were investigated. A quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional design was utilised. Participants were Malaysian employees working in manufacturing firms who completed a questionnaire. 384 completed questionnaires were collected from a sample of 500 resulting in a response rate of 76.8%. Data were analysed through descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, and conditional process analysis with PROCESS Model 7 using 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results found CSR to have a positive and significant effect on financial performance and employee engagement. Employee engagement had a positive and significant effect on financial performance and fully mediated the relationship between CSR and financial performance. Job autonomy was found to have no significant effect on the relationship between CSR and employee engagement but was found to have a positive and significant relationship with employee engagement. This study contributes to the field of CSR by providing evidence that employee engagement serves as an important internal mechanism through which responsible organisational practices affect financial performance. The findings of this study show that job design may play an important role in manufacturing contexts where there are more formal procedures and requirements for operation.

title: Validation of the Model of Financial Reporting Transparency and Accountability in Municipalities from the Perspective of Experts
summary: This study aimed to validate a multidimensional model of financial reporting transparency and accountability in municipalities from the perspective of academic and professional experts. The study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, relevant theoretical sources and previous studies were reviewed, and semi-structured interviews were conducted with experts in municipal accounting, auditing, financial management, and public-sector accountability. The interviews continued until theoretical saturation was achieved. The extracted codes were classified into dimensions, components, and indicators, and the reliability of coding was assessed through inter-coder agreement and Cohen’s kappa coefficient. In the quantitative phase, a researcher-made questionnaire based on the qualitative findings was developed and distributed among experts. The fuzzy Delphi technique was used to screen and confirm the indicators, and SmartPLS was applied to assess the measurement and structural validity of the proposed model. The inferential results confirmed the validity of a four-dimensional model including social, economic, organizational, and political dimensions. The inter-coder agreement was 89.6%, and Cohen’s kappa coefficient was 0.804, indicating strong coding reliability. Confirmatory factor analysis showed acceptable factor loadings for the retained indicators. Cronbach’s alpha values ranged from 0.719 to 0.833, composite reliability ranged from 0.735 to 0.846, and AVE values ranged from 0.586 to 0.641, confirming internal consistency and convergent validity. The structural model showed acceptable explanatory power, with R² values of 0.621 for the social dimension, 0.548 for the economic dimension, 0.482 for the organizational dimension, and 0.519 for the political dimension. The Q² values were positive for all dimensions, and the overall GOF index was 0.541, indicating strong model fit. The validated model demonstrates that municipal financial reporting transparency and accountability are multidimensional constructs shaped by social access, economic conditions, organizational capacity, and political-accountability relations. The model can serve as a diagnostic framework for improving reporting quality, public accountability, and financial governance in municipalities

title: Refleksi Nilai Altruisme Melalui Corporate Social Responsibility Terhadap Sustainable Consumption Behavior di Kota Pontianak
summary: Increasing consumer awareness of environmental issues has increased market demand for sustainable business practices in which reflected in corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives. CSR implementation in Indonesia continues to face challenges arising from consumer skepticism toward greenwashing practices driven by information disseminated on social media that affected sustainable consumption behavior. Pontianak City presents considerable potential for green economic development due to its predominantly young population although sustainable consumption practices remain relatively limited. This study aims to examine the role of CSR in promoting sustainable consumption behavior. A quantitative research approach was employed through an online survey of 105 Uniqlo consumers in Pontianak City, selected using purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4.0. The findings reveal that CSR has a positive and significant effect on customer advocacy (β = 0.628; p < 0.001), while customer advocacy significantly influences sustainable consumption behavior (β = 0.317; p = 0.004). Conversely, the direct effect of CSR on sustainable consumption behavior is not statistically significant (β = 0.134; p = 0.322), indicating that customer advocacy fully mediates this relationship (β = 0.199; p = 0.008). These findings highlight the relevance of customer advocacy as a mechanism through which CSR initiatives can foster sustainable consumption behavior. From a managerial perspective, the study highlights for companies to develop CSR strategies that promote active consumer engagement while ensuring transparency and accountability to mitigate potential greenwashing concerns in sustainability marketing campaigns.

title: Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence in Agricultural Marketing in Maharashtra: Opportunities and Challenges
summary: Abstract: Agricultural marketing in Maharashtra is undergoing a gradual transformation with the growing use of digital technologies and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Digital platforms, mobile applications, e-NAM, online market services, and digital payment systems are creating new ways for farmers to access market information, buyers, and prices. AI-based applications can further support agricultural marketing through price forecasting, demand analysis, market trend identification, and supply chain management. These developments have the potential to improve transparency, reduce information gaps, and support better marketing decisions among farmers. However, the adoption of these technologies also involves several challenges, including limited digital literacy, inadequate internet connectivity in rural areas, high technology costs, lack of technical knowledge, and difficulties faced by small and marginal farmers. This study examines the major opportunities and challenges associated with digital transformation and AI in agricultural marketing in Maharashtra. The study suggests that suitable digital infrastructure, farmer training, reliable market information, and accessible local-language technologies are essential for ensuring inclusive and effective use of digital technologies in agricultural marketing.

title: Accounting Compliance And Internal Audit in Public Financial Governance
summary: Penelitian ini mengkaji peran kepatuhan aturan akuntansi dalam memperkuat tata kelola keuangan publik, dengan audit internal berperan sebagai variabel moderator dalam pemerintah daerah. Penelitian ini membahas kesenjangan yang terus berlanjut antara peraturan keuangan formal dan implementasi substansialnya dalam pengelolaan keuangan publik daerah. Dengan menggunakan desain penelitian kuantitatif eksplanatori, penelitian ini dilakukan di Pemerintah Daerah Kabupaten Tapanuli Selatan, Indonesia. Data dikumpulkan dari 93 responden di 31 instansi pemerintah daerah dan dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kepatuhan akuntansi memiliki pengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap tata kelola keuangan publik. Audit internal juga menunjukkan pengaruh langsung yang signifikan dan, yang lebih penting, secara signifikan memperkuat hubungan antara kepatuhan akuntansi dan tata kelola keuangan publik. Koefisien determinasi menunjukkan bahwa model yang diusulkan memiliki daya penjelas yang moderat. Temuan ini menemukan bukti bahwa tata kelola keuangan publik yang efektif harus didorong oleh kepatuhan terhadap peraturan, serta adanya penguatan mekanisme pengawasan internal. Studi ini berkontribusi pada literatur akuntansi sektor publik dengan menawarkan model integratif yang menekankan sinergi strategis antara kepatuhan dan audit internal dalam meningkatkan tata kelola keuangan yang berkelanjutan di tingkat pemerintah daerah.

title: Management Dynamics Shaping the Adoption of Technology Driven Banking and Deposit Service in India
summary: There is an ongoing paradigm shift within the banking system of India due to advancements in digital public infrastructure, innovative regulatory measures, and changing customer expectations. This research paper attempts to study the dynamics of management such as governance, strategic leadership, regulatory interaction, and culture within organizations that define technology-based banking and depositing services in India. By analyzing the secondary data available through various regulatory, industry, and institutional reports for the years 2021–2026, the research evaluates the relationship between technological capabilities and managerial preparedness. The results indicate that the ability to adopt technology in banking is not about advanced technology but rather about the governance, oversight by the board of directors, and integration of legacy systems with digitized processes. The research proposes a management-focused approach to the understanding of digital transformation in banking, suggesting that sustainability of the deposit franchise is increasingly becoming contingent upon the quality of digital interaction rather than the availability of channels. Comparison of public and private sector banks indicates different approaches to adoption.

title: REQUIREMENTS ENGINEERING AND TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION FOR DIGITAL ACADEMIC MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS IN HIGHER EDUCATION
summary: The digital transformation of higher education requires integrated information systems capable of supporting academic planning, curriculum management, scheduling, electronic document circulation, reporting, and communication among institutional stakeholders A critical prerequisite for the successful development of such systems is the systematic identification, analysis, documentation, verification, and management of software requirements. This study examines a requirements engineering framework for an academic management information system in higher education and proposes a structured approach to the development of a Technical Specification (TS). The proposed framework distinguishes functional and non-functional requirements and incorporates stakeholder analysis, business process modelling, requirements prioritization, prototyping, verification, documentation, and lifecycle management. The study also considers the applicability of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, ISO/IEC 25010, IEEE 830, and GOST 34.602-89 as methodological references for technical specification development. The proposed approach establishes a common basis for communication between university administrators, academic departments, teachers, students, analysts, and software developers. title: Digital Innovation and Its Impact on Business Transformation in the Modern Economy
summary: Abstract Digital innovation has become a major force behind the transformation of modern businesses and economies. The rapid development of technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data analytics, the Internet of Things, blockchain, and automation has changed how organizations operate, create value, and interact with customers. Digital innovation is not limited to adopting new technologies; it also involves developing new products, services, processes, and business models. This research paper examines the concept of digital innovation and its impact on business transformation. It focuses on the major drivers of digital innovation, technologies that support it, benefits to organizations, challenges associated with implementation, and future trends. The study uses a descriptive and exploratory research methodology based primarily on secondary data collected from academic journals, books, research reports, and reliable online sources. The research finds that digital innovation can improve operational efficiency, customer experience, productivity, decision-making, and competitiveness. However, organizations face challenges such as cybersecurity threats, data privacy concerns, implementation costs, resistance to change, and a shortage of digital skills. The study concludes that organizations need appropriate strategies, skilled employees, effective leadership, and continuous innovation to successfully benefit from digital transformation.

title: Innovative Frontiers in Commerce: Emerging Trends and Future Opportunities
summary: Abstract The rapid advancement of technology, changing consumer preferences, and increasing global interconnectedness are transforming the traditional landscape of commerce. This research paper examines the innovative frontiers shaping modern commerce, with particular emphasis on emerging technologies, digital transformation, evolving business models, and changing consumer behaviour. Technologies such as artificial intelligence, blockchain, big data analytics, cloud computing, automation, and digital payment systems are creating new opportunities for businesses to improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experiences, and expand their market reach. The study also explores the growing significance of e-commerce, social commerce, omnichannel retailing, and sustainable business practices in shaping the future of commercial activities. Alongside these opportunities, businesses face challenges related to cybersecurity, data privacy, technological adoption, regulatory uncertainty, and the need for continuous innovation. The paper highlights how organizations can adapt to these developments by embracing technology-driven strategies, fostering innovation, and responding effectively to changing market demands. The study concludes that the future of commerce will be characterized by greater digital integration, personalization, sustainability, and technology-enabled business ecosystems. Understanding these emerging trends is essential for businesses, policymakers, researchers, and other stakeholders seeking to navigate the evolving commercial environment and capitalize on future opportunities.

title: The Influence of Accounting Information Systems and Internal Control Systems on the Quality of Medan City Government Financial Reports
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of accounting information systems and internal control systems on the quality of the Medan City Government’s financial reports. The quality of local government financial reporting is an important indicator of transparent, accountable, and reliable public governance. An adequate accounting information system is essential to support the accurate recording, processing, storage, and presentation of financial information. Meanwhile, an effective internal control system plays an important role in ensuring that financial management processes are carried out in accordance with applicable regulations while minimizing the risk of errors, irregularities, and inappropriate financial practices. This study employed an associative quantitative research approach. The research used primary data collected through questionnaires distributed to 63 respondents working in sub-district offices within the Medan City Government. The data collection process was conducted to obtain information regarding the implementation of accounting information systems, internal control systems, and the quality of financial reports. Data analysis was performed using multiple linear regression, t-tests, the F-test, and the coefficient of determination. The results indicate that accounting information systems have a positive and significant effect on the quality of financial reports, with a t-value of 2.828 and a significance value of 0.006. Internal control systems also have a positive and significant effect on financial report quality, with a t-value of 3.554 and a significance value of 0.001. Simultaneously, accounting information systems and internal control systems have a significant effect on the quality of financial reports, as indicated by an F-value of 111.209 with a significance value of less than 0.001. The coefficient of determination indicates that the two independent variables explain 84.2% of the variation in financial report quality, while the remaining 15.8% is explained by other factors outside the scope of this study. These findings emphasize that strengthening accounting information systems and internal control systems is essential for improving the quality, reliability, transparency, and accountability of local government financial reporting, particularly within the Medan City Government.

title: CSR and Green Knowledge Management as Drivers of Sustainable Performance: The Mediating Role of Green Innovation and the Moderating Effect of Top Management Commitment
summary: ABSTRACT In recent years, the dual pressures of economic development and environmental degradation have intensified the need for organizations to adopt environmentally sustainable practices. In this context, corporate social responsibility (CSR), green knowledge management (GKM), and green innovation (GI) have become critical mechanisms for enhancing sustainable performance, particularly within healthcare organizations operating in Palestine. Accordingly, this study seeks to examine the roles of CSR and GKM in shaping sustainable performance through the mediating influence of GI. In addition, the study evaluates the moderating effect of top management commitment (TMC) on the relationship between GI and sustainable performance. The proposed relationships are empirically tested using data collected from 181 respondents representing governmental and non‐governmental healthcare organizations in Palestine. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) is employed to assess the structural model and examine the hypothesized relationships. The findings reveal that CSR and GKM exert both direct and indirect effects on sustainable performance through GI. Notably, TMC does not significantly moderate the relationship between GI and sustainable performance. This finding suggests that, in resource‐constrained healthcare settings, managerial commitment alone may not be sufficient to strengthen the performance benefits associated with GI. One possible explanation is that the influence of managerial commitment depends on complementary organizational conditions, such as available resources, implementation capacity, delegated authority, and performance‐monitoring systems. Theoretically, the study identifies GI as an important complementary pathway through which CSR and GKM are associated with sustainable performance while showing that the role of TMC may be context‐dependent. Practically, the findings indicate that healthcare managers should complement leadership commitment with concrete implementation mechanisms. Contextually, the study extends sustainability research to Palestinian healthcare organizations operating under substantial resource and institutional constraints.

title: Digital Maturity in Higher Education: A Model and Design Principles for Institutional Transformation
summary: This study aims to develop a digital maturity model (DMM) specifically for higher education and to identify design principles emerging from the model development process. Recognizing that existing maturity frameworks rarely reflect the unique mission, governance, and stakeholder complexity of universities, this study addresses a conceptual and practical gap by integrating evidence from the literature, expert validation, and institutional piloting. A Design and Development Research methodology was employed. The development process combined a systematic literature review, document analysis, semi-structured interviews with 12 domain experts, a 25-week iterative expert panel process to refine the dimensions, levels, and indicators, and pilot implementation across 18 universities. The resulting model comprises five dimensions (individual, education, managerial processes, research, and infrastructure), 19 sub-dimensions, and 104 indicators, organized across five qualitative maturity levels: awareness, partial implementation, strategic implementation, integrated implementation, and cultural transformation. Four design principles were derived from the development process, emphasizing holistic dimensional coverage, clear and unambiguous level definitions, appropriately concrete indicators, and practical applicability. The model provides institutions with a structured instrument for assessing digital readiness, prioritizing transformation initiatives, informing strategic resource allocation, and benchmarking progress over time. An accompanying guideline is intended to facilitate stakeholder engagement and evidence-informed decision-making. Theoretically, the study contributes an empirically grounded and iteratively validated maturity model specific to higher education, while also offering design principles relevant to maturity model development and digital transformation in academic contexts.

title: ORGANIZATIONAL AND CULTURAL READINESS FACTORS FOR IMPLEMENTING AGILE MANAGEMENT IN REGIONAL TAX AUTHORITIES
summary: Abstract. This article examines the organizational and cultural readiness factors required for the effective implementation of Agile management in regional tax authorities. The primary objective of the study is to identify and theoretically substantiate the institutional, organizational, managerial, and human-capital factors that influence the adoption of flexible management approaches within the public tax administration system. The effectiveness of Agile management depends not only on restructuring administrative processes but also on the organizational culture, leadership commitment to change, employee autonomy in decision-making, teamwork, open communication, and the extent to which innovative initiatives are encouraged. The study systematizes the principal criteria for assessing organizational readiness for Agile transformation in regional tax authorities and analyzes the interrelationship between organizational flexibility, digital infrastructure, Agile competencies, leadership support, employee empowerment, and institutional resistance to change. Particular attention is given to the importance of creating a collaborative organizational environment in which employees can respond rapidly to changing regulatory, technological, and service-delivery requirements. The article also substantiates the potential of gradual Agile implementation to improve the responsiveness, transparency, citizen orientation, and overall efficiency of tax administration. The findings provide a conceptual basis for developing practical recommendations aimed at establishing a modern, adaptive, digitally oriented, and results-driven management model within regional tax authorities. Keywords: Agile management, regional tax authorities, organizational readiness, organizational culture, leadership support, employee autonomy, digital transformation, adaptive management.

title: Implementation of A Digital Warehouse and Inventory Management System to Support Stock Management Effectiveness in the Freshmart Retail Business Simulation
summary: Digital transformation has accelerated the adoption of Warehouse Management Systems (WMS) and Inventory Management Systems (IMS) as effective solutions for improving inventory management in retail businesses. This study aims to analyze the implementation of a digital Warehouse and Inventory Management System and evaluate its contribution to stock management effectiveness in the FreshMart retail business simulation. A qualitative descriptive approach was employed through an operational simulation using a ready-to-use Warehouse and Inventory Management application. Data were collected through observations of application usage, documentation of simulation results, and evaluation of system implementation in inventory recording, supplier management, stock monitoring, inbound and outbound inventory transactions, as well as low-stock and expired-item monitoring. The results indicate that the system successfully integrates operational data into a single platform, enhances real-time inventory visibility, simplifies stock monitoring, supports reorder decision-making, and reduces administrative errors compared to manual recording methods. However, because data entry is still performed manually, the potential for human error has not been completely eliminated. This study concludes that a ready-to-use Warehouse and Inventory Management application provides a practical and cost-effective digital logistics solution for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and small-to-medium retail businesses. Nevertheless, further development of automation features is necessary to improve data accuracy and operational effectiveness.

title: Climate risk and corporate carbon emissions: a cross-country study
summary: Purpose This study examines whether country-level climate risk influences corporate carbon emissions. It also investigates how financial slack shapes firms’ responses to climate risk. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of 10,834 firm-year observations from 42 countries over the period from 2010 to 2024, we applied regression models on panel data estimated with robust standard errors. We also addressed endogeneity using propensity score matching, two-stage least squares and difference-in-differences approaches. Findings The findings show that firms exposed to climate risk exhibit higher carbon emissions, consistent with the resource-constraint perspective. Indeed, climate-related risks can hinder corporate environmental performance by limiting the financial capacity required to implement sustainable carbon reduction strategies. This positive association is significantly weaker among firms with greater financial flexibility, proxied by long-term and short-term financial slack, and significantly stronger among financially constrained firms. This positive association is also attenuated in the post–Paris Agreement period (2016 onward), among firms with a sustainability committee and among those operating under more stringent environmental policy regimes. These results point to institutional pressure and internal governance as additional channels that offset the positive effect of climate risk on carbon emissions. Originality/value This study adds to the literature on the consequences of climate risk by providing new insights into the climate risk–carbon emissions relationship in a cross-country study. It also identifies financial flexibility, sustainability governance and institutional pressures (environmental policy stringency and the Paris Agreement) as mitigating channels. This offers valuable guidance for policymakers by highlighting the role of financial capacity, corporate governance and supportive policy frameworks in enhancing firms’ resilience to climate-related shocks and facilitating the transition to a low-carbon economy.

title: Green governance effects of Open Government Data on corporate ESG performance
summary: This study examines how the rollout of Open Government Data (OGD) platforms in China affects corporate ESG performance. We find that OGD improves corporate ESG performance. The effect operates through stronger external monitoring and increased green innovation, as OGD expands access to key government data. Additionally, the effect is stronger in regions with high external monitoring and strict legal systems. It is also stronger for large firms, pollution-intensive industries, and areas with better OGD infrastructure. We also find that OGD improves firms’ ESG practices. This study adds to ESG research and provides evidence for policy.

title: Going Concern as an Epistemic Foundation of the Accounting-Audit-Taxation Relationship: Econometric Evidence and Interpretation through Marginal Effects
summary: In the current context of increasing requirements regarding the transparency of financial reporting, the going-concern principle exceeds its strictly accounting dimension and becomes an epistemic reference point for the credibility of financial information, audit quality and the sustainability of business models. The study develops an interdisciplinary framework by investigating going concern from the perspective of the relationship between accounting, taxation and audit, with the aim of identifying the factors that influence the probability of maintaining the financial viability of companies listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange during 2018-2024. The research methodology uses the Ordered Logit econometric model, which is appropriate for the ordinal nature of the dependent variable concerning going concern, structured on three levels: discontinuity risk, moderate uncertainty and full continuity. To deepen the interpretation of the results, Average Marginal Effects (AME) were estimated, allowing the variation in the probabilities associated with each going-concern category to be quantified according to changes in the significant predictors. The empirical results reveal consistent and statistically significant marginal effects generated by the debt ratio, auditor type and audit opinion. The research contributes to the literature by integrating an epistemic perspective on the accounting-taxation-audit relationship with an applied econometric approach based on the interpretation of marginal effects.

title: Digital adoption and firm capability: Substitution effects in productivity across developing economies
summary: This study examines how digital adoption interacts with firm capability to shape productivity outcomes across developing economies. Much of the existing literature emphasizes complementarity between digital technologies and firm capabilities, suggesting that firms with stronger capabilities benefit more from digital transformation. This study offers an alternative perspective by showing that digital adoption may also function as a capability equalizer under certain conditions. Using firm-level data from the World Bank Enterprise Surveys covering 7,057 firms, regression analysis with interaction terms is employed to assess how the effects of digital adoption vary with firm capability. The results indicate that both digital adoption and firm capability are positively associated with productivity, while their interaction is negative and statistically significant. This pattern implies that the marginal productivity gains from digitalization are larger for firms with lower levels of capability. Digital technologies therefore appear to partially compensate for internal capability constraints rather than simply reinforcing existing advantages. Additional analysis suggests that this equalizing effect is primarily driven by skill-related capability, whereas managerial capability remains largely complementary. The productivity effects of digital adoption are also more pronounced among small and medium-sized enterprises. These findings highlight the role of digital technologies not only in enhancing firm performance but also in reshaping the relationship between capability and productivity. Under certain conditions, digitalization may reduce the dependence on internal capability and may help narrow productivity disparities across firms.

title: Environmental, Social and Governance Performance and Firm Value: A Bibliometric Review of Intellectual Structure and Emerging Research Trends (2015-2025)
summary: The issues of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors have gained much attention in terms of firm valuation and investment decisions. Although ESG has been extensively studied over the years, there is a lack of understanding in terms of the intellectual structure and thematic development of the relationship between ESG and firm value. To bridge this gap, this paper seeks to conduct a bibliometric analysis of the body of literature about ESG–firm value relationships from the year 2015 to 2025. The research will utilise a data set of 589 journal papers that were retrieved from the Scopus database for the purpose of investigating the publication dynamics, prominent contributors, citation network, and the intellectual/conceptual structure of the field. From the analysis of the science mapping results, it can be deduced that there are four major streams of research: (1) relationship between ESG performance and firm value; (2) sustainability disclosures and transparency; (3) corporate governance structure; and (4) consequences of ESG factors on financial performance such as cost of capital and investment efficiency. In addition, through co-citations and bibliographic coupling, it is evident that the theories upon which the body of knowledge is built include not only finance but also stakeholder theory, agency theory, and sustainable perspectives. The contribution of this paper to the literature on ESG-firm value lies in synthesizing the existing works on the subject matter.

title: PENGARUH ESG SCORE DAN GREEN INNOVATION TERHADAP MARKET VALUE OF EQUITY PADA PERUSAHAAN SEKTOR ENERGI YANGTERDAFTAR PADA BURSA EFEK INDONESIATAHUN 2020-2024
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh parsial dan simultan dari skor Lingkungan, Sosial, dan Tata Kelola (ESG) dan inovasi hijau terhadap nilai pasar ekuitas perusahaan sektor energi yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (IDX) pada tahun 2020–2024. Studi kausal-eksploratif ini menerapkan teori pemangku kepentingan dan pandangan berbasis sumber daya. Data yang digunakan adalah data panel dari 28 perusahaan sampel dengan 140 observasi yang dianalisis dengan teknik Fixed Effect Model (FEM) yang telah dikoreksi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengungkapan skor ESG tidak secara signifikan memengaruhi nilai pasar ekuitas, menunjukkan bahwa transparansi narasi keberlanjutan belum mendapat respons luas dari investor sektor energi. Di sisi lain, implementasi inovasi hijau memiliki pengaruh positif dan agak substansial, yang berarti bahwa pasar menganggap penerapan aktual teknologi ramah lingkungan sebagai kemampuan strategis untuk mengurangi risiko non-finansial. Selain itu, pengungkapan ESG dan inovasi hijau memiliki dampak yang cukup besar terhadap nilai pasar ekuitas secara bersamaan. Pelaporan ESG saja bukanlah pendorong pasar terbaik, tetapi kombinasi transparansi tata kelola dan investasi inovasi hijau dapat mengirimkan sinyal positif yang kuat kepada investor dan meningkatkan nilai pasar ekuitas perusahaan.

title: Capital Intensity and Accrual-Based Earnings Management in Vietnamese Listed Non-Financial Firms
summary: Because accrual accounting relies on managerial judgment, firms’ asset structures may shape the opportunities for discretion in reported earnings. This study examines the relationship between capital intensity and accrual-based earnings management among Vietnamese listed non-financial firms. Drawing on an unbalanced panel constructed from corporate financial statements, the study estimates discretionary accruals using the industry-year Modified Jones model and uses their absolute values to capture the magnitude of earnings management. The analysis employs firm and year fixed effects with firm-clustered standard errors, complemented by feasible generalized least squares and Driscoll–Kraay inference. The findings indicate a consistently negative association between capital intensity and absolute discretionary accruals after accounting for observable firm characteristics. This evidence extends earlier sector-specific research and highlights the relevance of tangible asset composition to accrual behavior in an emerging market. The findings suggest that investors, creditors, and auditors should consider asset structure alongside other financial indicators when assessing earnings-related reporting risks, without treating capital intensity as a standalone measure of reporting quality or the observed association as causal.

title: Opinion: Decisions without documents: Records continuity and evidential accountability in agentic supply chains
summary: Agentic artificial intelligence is taking supply chain software from recommendation to execution. Planning and procurement agents now execute replenishment orders, reallocate freight, and negotiate with suppliers based on delegated powers, all without simultaneous human approval. Virtually every organization maintains the records of such activities as log files, subject only to IT retention policies until the files are no longer useful for diagnostic purposes and then disposed of. This opinion article contends that such treatment misclassifies what is, in substance, evidence of business transactions. An agent-executed decision that commits expenditure, alters a contractual position or redistributes risk across trading partners creates obligations that auditors, counterparties, regulators and courts may later test, and its trace therefore meets the functional definition of a record. Drawing on records continuum theory, the article follows a single agent decision across the dimensions of creation, capture, organisation and pluralisation and locates the points at which it leaves any recordkeeping regime. It then specifies the attributes of a trustworthy decision record in terms of reliability, authenticity and integrity, and proposes a governance arrangement in which records and information managers hold design authority over decision records alongside IT, procurement, legal and audit functions. The argument is addressed to information professionals in commercial settings who will increasingly be asked to evidence what an agent did, and on whose authority.

title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation as Drivers of Sustainable and Inclusive Economic Growth: A Roadmap for Viksit Bharat @2047
summary: Abstract Entrepreneurship and innovation are increasingly recognised as important forces behind economic transformation, employment generation and social development. For a country such as India, which is working towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, the role of entrepreneurs extends beyond establishing new businesses. Entrepreneurs identify unmet needs, introduce new products and services, create employment, improve productivity and contribute to the formalisation of economic activity. Innovation, in turn, provides the means through which entrepreneurial ideas are converted into practical and scalable solutions. This paper examines the role of entrepreneurship and innovation in promoting sustainable and inclusive economic growth in India, with particular reference to the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047. The study is conceptual and is based on secondary information obtained from government publications, Startup India resources and relevant academic literature. The paper discusses the relationship between entrepreneurial activity, innovation, employment generation, digital transformation, social inclusion and sustainable development. It also examines the emerging startup ecosystem in India and the importance of government initiatives in creating an enabling environment for entrepreneurs. The analysis suggests that entrepreneurship and innovation can contribute significantly to economic development when supported by access to finance, appropriate skills, digital infrastructure, research and development, intellectual property protection, market access and institutional support. However, challenges such as uneven access to resources, limited entrepreneurial capabilities, fear of failure, regulatory complexity and the digital divide continue to affect entrepreneurial participation. The paper argues that achieving the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision requires a broader understanding of entrepreneurship that includes rural enterprises, women entrepreneurs, social enterprises, student innovators, technology-based startups and traditional businesses adopting innovative practices. The paper concludes by proposing a framework for strengthening entrepreneurship and innovation as instruments of inclusive, resilient and sustainable national development.

title: Directors' Remuneration Intensity, Board Independence and Firm Value in Kenya
summary: Background: Directors’ remuneration and board independence are important aspects of corporate governance that may influence firm value. However, empirical evidence regarding their relationships with firm value remains inconclusive, particularly in emerging markets. Limited research has examined whether board independence moderates the relationship between directors’ remuneration intensity and market-based firm value among listed companies in Kenya. Aims: To examine the relationship between directors' remuneration intensity and firm value, and to establish whether board independence moderates this relationship among companies listed in an emerging market. Study Design: A quantitative, longitudinal panel study using secondary data. Place and Duration of Study: Companies listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange, Kenya, over the period 2010–2021. Methodology: A balanced panel of 492 firm-year observations from 41 listed companies was analysed. Firm value was measured using Tobin's Q; directors' remuneration intensity was measured as directors' remuneration divided by sales; and board independence was measured as the percentage of independent directors. Two-way (firm and year) fixed-effects regressions with firm-clustered standard errors were estimated, complemented by wild cluster bootstrap inference, marginal-effects analysis and robustness tests covering outliers, lagged regressors, additional governance controls, sector-by-year effects and sub-samples. Results: Directors' remuneration intensity was not significantly associated with Tobin's Q (β = −0.014, P = .15), and neither was board independence (β = −0.002, P = .81). The interaction between the two was negative and of borderline significance (β = −0.0024, P = .06; wild bootstrap P = .03), such that the association between remuneration intensity and firm value became negative only when independent directors exceeded approximately 82% of the board. This pattern was concentrated in 2020–2021 and did not survive sector-by-year effects, the exclusion of financial firms or lagged regressors. Conclusion: Sales-scaled director remuneration does not appear to convey value-relevant information to investors in this market, and high formal board independence does not convert director pay into shareholder value. Remuneration committees should link director fees more closely to performance, and regulators should prioritise remuneration transparency over higher numerical independence thresholds.

title: BEYOND TEACHING: DOSEN PENGGERAK SEBAGAI PEMIMPIN TRANSFORMASIONAL DALAM PENDIDIKAN TINGGI DI ERA ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
summary: Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah mendorong perubahan mendasar dalam pendidikan tinggi sehingga menuntut rekonstruksi peran dosen dari penyampai pengetahuan menjadi pemimpin transformasi akademik. Namun, sebagian besar penelitian masih berfokus pada adopsi teknologi, kompetensi digital, atau kebijakan institusional, sehingga belum menjelaskan secara komprehensif peran dosen sebagai pemimpin transformasional dalam menghadapi perubahan tersebut. Penelitian ini bertujuan merekonstruksi konsep dosen penggerak melalui perspektif Transformational Leadership Theory serta menghasilkan kerangka konseptual yang relevan bagi pendidikan tinggi pada era AI. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis library research. Data diperoleh dari buku, artikel ilmiah bereputasi, dan dokumen kebijakan, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan teknik content analysis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa transformasi pendidikan tinggi tidak cukup dilakukan melalui integrasi teknologi, tetapi memerlukan perubahan paradigma mengenai kepemimpinan akademik dosen. Berdasarkan sintesis berbagai literatur, penelitian ini menghasilkan Beyond Teaching Framework, yaitu model konseptual yang menempatkan dosen penggerak sebagai pemimpin transformasional melalui enam dimensi utama, yaitu Building Academic Culture, Empowering Learners, Yielding Research Innovation, Orchestrating Digital Transformation, Nurturing Ethical Intelligence, dan Driving Institutional Change. Kerangka tersebut memperluas implementasi Transformational Leadership Theory dalam konteks pendidikan tinggi dengan mengintegrasikan kepemimpinan akademik, inovasi digital, pemanfaatan AI secara etis, dan transformasi kelembagaan ke dalam satu model konseptual yang utuh. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi teoretis melalui rekonstruksi konsep dosen penggerak dari perspektif berbasis kompetensi menuju kepemimpinan transformasional, sekaligus menawarkan implikasi praktis bagi perguruan tinggi dalam merancang kebijakan pengembangan dosen yang adaptif terhadap tantangan era AI.

title: GOOD CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND FIRM SIZE AS DETERMINANTS OF FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY: FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE AS MODERATOR
summary: This study aimed to examine the effect of Good Corporate Governance and firm size on financial sustainability, with financial performance as a moderating variable, in Islamic commercial banks listed with the Financial Services Authority in Indonesia during the 2021–2025 period. The study employed a quantitative approach with an associative-causal design. The population consisted of all Islamic commercial banks registered with the Financial Services Authority, and a sample of 8 banks was selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 40 firm-year observations over five years. Secondary data were collected from annual reports and corporate governance reports. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression and Moderated Regression Analysis with the assistance of SPSS version 25. The results showed that Good Corporate Governance had no significant effect on financial sustainability, with a significance value of 0.517. Firm size had no significant effect on financial sustainability, with a significance value of 0.125. Financial performance did not moderate the relationship between firm size and financial sustainability, with a significance value above 0.05. However, financial performance significantly and positively moderated the relationship between Good Corporate Governance and financial sustainability, with a significance value of 0.008 and an increase in the adjusted coefficient of determination from −0.015 to 0.143. These findings implied that the effectiveness of Good Corporate Governance in ensuring financial sustainability depended heavily on the bank's ability to generate healthy financial performance, while firm size alone did not guarantee financial sustainability in Indonesian Islamic commercial banks.

title: METHODOLOGICAL APPROACHES TO ASSESSING CORPORATE GOVERNANCE EFFECTIVENESS IN MODERN ECONOMIC CONDITIONS
summary: The study systematizes approaches to assessing corporate governance and develops a reproducible diagnostic framework for joint-stock companies. Comparative, institutional and systems analysis, documentary review and multicriteria assessment are applied. A two-layer framework distinguishes formal compliance from the actual functioning of governance mechanisms. Indicators, normalization rules, aggregation procedures and sensitivity checks are specified. A hypothetical numerical example demonstrates diagnostic use but does not constitute empirical evidence about Uzbek firms. The framework may support internal governance reviews and comparative assessments when verifiable company-level data are available.

summary: The rapid development of digital technologies is transforming modern economies by creating new mechanisms of production, distribution, consumption, and public administration. This article examines the theoretical foundations and current trends of the digital economy, focusing on the experience of the Republic of Uzbekistan. Particular attention is given to the "Digital Uzbekistan – 2030" strategy, digital infrastructure, e-government, digital finance, e-commerce, the IT sector, and human capital development. The study applies systematic, comparative, and institutional approaches, as well as the analysis of statistical and regulatory information. The findings show that Uzbekistan has established important institutional and technological foundations for digital transformation. However, challenges remain, including the digital divide, a shortage of qualified specialists, cybersecurity risks, unequal regional access to digital infrastructure, and regulatory gaps. The study proposes strengthening digital infrastructure, developing digital skills, expanding the application of artificial intelligence and big data, supporting digital entrepreneurship, and promoting international digital integration. title: Advancing Digital Banking in Albania: Trust, Financial Literacy and Regulatory Readiness in the FinTech Ecosystem
summary: Digital transformation is reshaping banking systems worldwide, yet the pace and depth of adoption remain uneven across emerging financial markets. Albania has made visible progress in electronic payments, online banking access and regulatory alignment with European digital finance standards; however, the transition from formal access to sustained digital banking adoption remains incomplete. This study examines the factors influencing digital banking and FinTech adoption in Albania, with a specific focus on consumer trust, financial literacy, perceived barriers and regulatory readiness. The paper applies a mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected through a structured consumer survey with 151 respondents and analyzed through descriptive statistics and Spearman correlation analysis. Qualitative evidence was gathered through 15 semi-structured interviews with representatives from commercial banks, electronic money institutions, public institutions, regulators, sectoral organizations and academic experts. Thematic analysis was used to identify common institutional, technological and regulatory patterns. The findings show that digital banking services are widely accessible, but usage intensity remains moderate. Weekly and monthly use are more common than daily use, while trust, financial knowledge and perceived barriers significantly shape adoption patterns. The correlation analysis indicates a positive relationship between financial knowledge and digital banking use, and a negative relationship between perceived barriers and usage. Interview findings reveal six major themes: digital transformation as a strategic priority, Bank–FinTech cooperation, regulatory adaptation, cybersecurity and data protection, financial education, and an optimistic but conditional outlook toward 2030. The study contributes to the literature on digital financial inclusion in emerging markets by integrating consumer-level evidence with institutional and regulatory perspectives. It argues that Albania’s digital banking transition requires not only technological investment, but also trust-building, digital financial education, cybersecurity, regulatory innovation and stronger cooperation between banks, FinTech actors, regulators and academia.

title: Can the green intellectual capital dimension, in conjunction with fintech adoption, achieve business sustainability?
summary: MSMEs are important pillars of the Indonesian economy as economic drivers, but they also have social and environmental responsibilities in supporting sustainable development. This study aims to analyze the green intellectual capital model, which not only considers profits but also contributes to environmental sustainability by leveraging fintech, thereby achieving business sustainability across economic, social, and environmental dimensions. This research method uses a quantitative approach, collecting primary data through questionnaires and analyzing them using SEM-PLS, with a sample of 220 businesses. The results of the study indicate that green intellectual capital has a significant influence on fintech adoption and on sustainability performance in all aspects, i.e., economic, social, and environmental. Fintech adoption has a significant influence on economic and social sustainability performance, but not significantly on environmental performance. Fintech adoption can mediate the effect of green intellectual capital on economic and social performance. Still, it cannot mediate the effect of green intellectual capital on environmental performance among MSMEs in the Serikat Usaha Muhammadiyah (SUMU) community of East Java. To achieve scale-up for MSMEs, specific policies are needed to direct the use of green fintech in company operations, thereby achieving a significant impact in realizing sustainable businesses, such as the use of environmentally friendly raw materials and products, energy efficiency, and access to green financing.

title: KONTAMINASI KRISIS GREEN FINANCE TERHADAP AKTIVITAS SEKTOR PERBANKAN INDONESIA
summary: The banking sector performance is key to mitigating the negative effects of the green finance crisis. This study examines and detects the contamination of external and internal financial pressures, which resulted in the green finance crisis. Using Bank Indonesia Report data from 2010 – 2025 (time series), with the Ed Waves Index development model using E-Views Version 9. The results found that external pressures (Interest Rates and Exchange Rates) and internal pressures (Deposits and Credit) have the strong potential to cause a green finance crisis, through an increase in Non-Performing Loans, which has an effect on weakening financial stability. Therefore, a balance is needed between the banking intermediary function in managing financial circulation, as part of increasing the effectiveness of green finance distribution in the industrial sector. This aims to achieve an optimal balance in the financial ecosystem and the environmental ecosystem, as an effort to prevent the negative effects of a more acute green finance crisis. Furthermore, strong interconnection is needed between the Central Bank, the banking sector, and the industrial sector for a more optimal integration of financial circulation management, in creating a sustainable balance between the financial and the environmental ecosystem.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF E-INVOICES GENERATED FROM CASH REGISTERS (POS E-INVOICES): EXPERIENCES FROM EAST ASIA AND LESSONS FOR PROMOTING THE DIGITAL ECONOMY IN VIETNAM
summary: This paper examines the digital transformation of tax administration in Vietnam, with a focus on the mandatory implementation of electronic invoices generated from cash registers (POS e-invoicing) under Decree 70/2025/ND-CP. Although this policy is designed to enhance financial transparency and enable continuous transaction controls (CTC), its rapid rollout has encountered notable resistance from small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and business households. Drawing on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), and recent policy reports and empirical studies from the 2025–2026 period, this study identifies key barriers to adoption. These include high compliance costs, Application Programming Interface (API) incompatibility between legacy accounting systems and tax platforms, and behavioural resistance to real-time financial transparency. To contextualize these challenges, the study conducts a structured comparative analysis of selected East Asian economies. The findings highlight the role of financial incentives in South Korea, centralized technological infrastructure in China, and a phased and flexible transition approach in Japan. Based on these insights, the paper argues that administrative mandates alone are insufficient to ensure effective implementation. It proposes a comprehensive policy framework for Vietnam that integrates technological standardization, targeted financial support, and behavioural incentive mechanisms. These measures are expected to reduce implementation frictions, enhance voluntary tax compliance, and support the sustainable development of the national digital economy.

title: Automation of Accounting and Management Accounting Using Digital Platforms and Artificial Intelligence: The Role of Blockchain Technology in Enhancing Efficiency and Transparency
summary: Purpose: The purpose of this paper is to examine the use of digital platforms to automate financial and management accounting functions, with particular focus on the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain technology. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study adopts a qualitative secondary data research methodology using existing scholarly materials, industry reports, and case studies to evaluate the effectiveness of these technologies in improving accounting operations. The sample of 27 publications (2014–2026) was obtained from online academic databases such as Google Scholar, ScienceDirect and JSTOR, and examined by thematic analysis. Research Limitation: The study identifies high implementation costs, technical complexity, and data privacy and cybersecurity issues as the main challenges, indicating the need for further research on scalable and cost-effective solutions. Findings: The findings indicate that AI-driven automation enhances precision, reduces human error, and supports more accurate decision-making through instant data analysis. Blockchain technology increases the transparency, security, and reliability of financial transactions through its decentralised and immutable structure. Practical Implication: The adoption of AI and blockchain in accounting systems offers considerable advantages for organisations, particularly in improving operational efficiency and supporting strategic management. Social Implication: The wider adoption of digital technologies contributes to more transparent, secure, and reliable accounting practices in the modern business environment. Originality/Value: The article examines AI and blockchain in management accounting tasks, such as forecasting and decision support, which have received less attention than auditing and financial reporting, and highlights future research directions for the development of scalable solutions that can be adopted at lower cost.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Financial Performance in Moroccan Startups: The Mediating Effect of Financial Reporting Quality
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping financial information systems by automating accounting processes, expanding analytical capabilities, and supporting managerial decision-making. However, evidence remains limited regarding the mechanisms through which AI adoption contributes to financial performance, particularly among startups operating in emerging economies. Drawing on the Resource-Based View and rational decision-making theory, this study examines the effect of AI adoption on the financial performance of Moroccan startups and tests the mediating role of financial reporting quality. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was adopted. Data were collected through a structured online questionnaire distributed to executives, financial managers, and management controllers working in Moroccan startups. Of 160 questionnaires distributed, 125 complete responses were retained for analysis. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings show that AI adoption positively affects financial reporting quality (β = 0.792, p < 0.001) and financial performance (β = 0.441, p < 0.001). Financial reporting quality also has a positive effect on financial performance (β = 0.472, p < 0.001). In addition, the indirect effect of AI adoption on financial performance through financial reporting quality is positive and significant (β = 0.373, p < 0.001), indicating complementary partial mediation. These findings suggest that AI creates value not only through direct operational and strategic improvements but also, by enhancing the reliability, timeliness, and usefulness of financial information for decision-making. The study contributes to the literature by integrating technological, informational, and performance-related mechanisms within an underexplored Moroccan startup context. Practically, it highlights the importance of combining investments in AI with robust financial reporting processes, data-management practices, and internal control mechanisms.

title: The Fourth Chokepoint: Administrative Standardization as Process Control in China's Rare Earth Separation Industry
summary: Earlier work on rare earth supply chain resilience identifies three chokepoints, geology, processing capital expenditure, and separation learning curves. This preprint proposes a fourth, administrative control of the process envelope, meaning who may run a separation cascade, at what volume, on which feed, to which technical reference, under whose data, and with what permission to transfer know-how. Using public records from 2011 to October 2026, it describes six coupled layers of control in China's rare earth sector (volume, structure, technical envelope, information, boundary, and buffer) and maps them onto a process control analogy. Verified findings include the 2024 company level split of mining and separation quotas, the placement of the entire ion-adsorption mining quota in one company, the 2025 shift to undisclosed quotas and total volume control, and the concentration of imported feed in two border supply lines. The paper audits a broader compilation of reported mechanisms against public sources. Every claim is graded by evidence tier in an appendix, errors are corrected, and unverified items are listed as open requests for verification. The central thesis is presented as a hypothesis with rival explanations and falsifiable predictions, not as an established result. Corrections and primary sources are welcome.

title: GREEN FINANCE AND SME INCLUSION IN ZIMBABWE: EVIDENCE FROM THE MANUFACTURING SECTOR IN BINDURA
summary: Green finance is increasingly recognized as a central instrument for advancing climate mitigation and sustainable development, yet its distributive effects remain poorly understood in developing economies where small and medium enterprises (SMEs) dominate industrial activity. This study examines access to green finance among manufacturing SMEs in Bindura, Zimbabwe, identifying the structural determinants of inclusion and the institutional mechanisms driving exclusion. A mixed-methods approach is employed, combining quantitative survey data from 36 manufacturing firms analyzed through binary logistic regression with qualitative evidence from key informant interviews with financial institutions and policy actors. The results reveal that green finance access is highly selective: firm size, collateral availability, and awareness are significant positive predictors of access, while smaller and asset-constrained firms are systematically excluded. Green finance is predominantly delivered through conventional asset-based lending models underpinned by risk perceptions that disadvantage SMEs, reinforcing credit rationing and information asymmetry. These findings challenge the assumption that green finance is inherently inclusive and suggest that current frameworks risk entrenching a dual transition in which only better-positioned firms participate. Policy reforms should prioritize risk-sharing mechanisms, SME-adapted financial instruments, and targeted information dissemination to ensure a more equitable and effective green transition.

title: Supply Chain Management and Logistics: How Important Is Interconnection for Business Success?
summary: Purpose - This paper explains why interconnection - the coordinated linking of information, material, financial and decision flows across internal functions and external partners - is a first-order determinant of business success, and specifies when, where and how much firms should integrate. Design/methodology/approach - We synthesise the theoretical and empirical literature on supply chain integration (SCI) and logistics, build an integrative framework, and formalise it with four analytical models: a moderated integration–performance equation, published closed-form bounds on bullwhip amplification under centralised and decentralised demand information, a safety-stock elasticity decomposition, and a new optimal-interconnection model solved in closed form with the Lambert W function. No simulated or hypothetical data are presented as evidence; all quantitative curves are exact outputs of stated models. Findings - Large-sample studies and meta-analyses consistently associate integration with superior performance, most strongly for internal integration and for firms that integrate toward suppliers and customers simultaneously. Our models show that the value of sharing demand information grows convexly with the number of stages and lead times; that the lever a firm should prioritise (information sharing versus logistics integration) is determined by a simple dominance condition; and that the value of interconnection is inverted-U-shaped, with an optimal depth that rises with uncertainty and falls with integration cost. Originality/value - The paper unifies behavioural, economic and operations-research arguments into seven testable propositions, derives a closed-form optimal level of interconnection that formalises the over-integration critique, and offers a diagnostic guide and an empirical test design for researchers and managers. Keywords: supply chain integration; logistics; interconnection; information sharing; bullwhip effect; safety stock; optimal integration; firm performance.

title: The Impact of Professionalism (Itqan) on the Quality of Financial Reporting in Islamic Financial Institutions
summary: This study aims to examine the relationship between professionalism (itqan) and financial reporting quality in Sharia financial institutions in Indonesia. Employing a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design, data were collected from 85 respondents through structured questionnaires using a five-point Likert scale. Professionalism (itqan) was measured through professional competence, accuracy, responsibility, integrity, work discipline, and commitment to excellence, while financial reporting quality was assessed through relevance, faithful representation, comparability, verifiability, timeliness, understandability, and transparency. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, validity and reliability tests, regression diagnostics, and simple linear regression with SPSS version 25. The results indicate that professionalism (itqan) has a positive and statistically significant relationship with financial reporting quality, with a regression coefficient of 0.303, a t-value of 3.391, and a significance value of 0.001. The coefficient of determination (R² = 0.122) indicates that professionalism explains 12.2% of the variation in perceived financial reporting quality. These findings highlight the importance of integrating Islamic professional ethics with technical competence to strengthen financial reporting practices. The study contributes to Islamic accounting literature by positioning itqan as a distinct professional construct associated with financial transparency, reliability, and institutional accountability.

title: Green Accounting and Profitability of Listed Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria
summary: This study examined Green Accounting and Profitability of Listed Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria, and considered how green accounting employed by Nigerian firms would significantly impact investors’ return in the long run. The study used ex-post facto research design that covered annual financial report from 2020 to 2024 as listed on Nigerian Exchange Group as at December 31, 2024, and data were analysed through descriptive statistics, regression and Correlation. The findings displayed that return on assets showed significant effect with co-efficient of -41.658 and p-value of 0.035; returns on equity displayed positive but insignificant with co-efficient of 29.182 and P-value of 0.475, and net profit margin showed co-efficient of 265.778 and P-value of 0.001 at 1% level. The study concluded that green accounting was a significant approach that could be used to get more returns on asset utilisation and operational effectiveness. It was recommended that environmental costs should be well managed, adhering to regulatory framework and given tax incentive to firms that involved in sustainability.

title: Innovation in Financial Performance and CSR: Their Impact on Stock Returns in Indonesian Government and Private Banks
summary: General Background The capital market is an essential intermediary for connecting investors with entities seeking funds, wherein stock return serves as a critical measure of investment performance. Specific Background Indonesian state-owned banks, primarily represented by the Association of State-Owned Banks (HIMBARA) and Regional Development Banks (BPD), operate with dual mandates that encompass commercial profitability and government economic development objectives, distinct from private banks. Knowledge Gap Although numerous studies evaluate banking performance, limited empirical analysis exists on how market-based indicators versus accounting metrics and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) simultaneously explain the variations in stock returns across distinct banking ownership structures in Indonesia. Aims This study investigates the effect of financial performance—measured by Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR), Net Profit Margin (NPM), Return on Equity (ROE), and Price to Earnings Ratio (PER)—and CSR on the stock returns of HIMBARA and regional banks compared to private banks from 2020 to 2024. Results Utilizing the Common Effect Model (CEM) on 85 firm-year observations from 17 banks, the analysis indicates that CAR and NPM exert a negative, albeit insignificant, effect on stock returns. While ROE presents a positive but negligible relationship, CSR demonstrates a negative and insignificant association. Conversely, PER significantly and positively dictates stock returns, serving as the sole explanatory variable with substantial impact. Furthermore, independent-samples t-tests revealed no statistically significant divergence in stock returns between private and state-owned banks. Novelty This study highlights that market valuation, specifically PER, supersedes traditional capital adequacy and CSR disclosures in driving investor behavior within the Indonesian banking sector. Implications Bank management should prioritize transparent market-oriented financial communication and sustainable capital utilization over nominal CSR activities, while future models must incorporate macroeconomic and market-sentiment factors to capture comprehensive stock volatility. HIGHLIGHTS The Price to Earnings Ratio (PER) significantly and positively drives stock returns, overshadowing traditional accounting metrics like capital adequacy and profitability. Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) disclosures exhibit a negative and statistically insignificant effect on banking stock returns during the observed period. Bank ownership status (state-owned versus private) does not result in a statistically significant difference in realized stock returns for investors. KEYWORDS Stock Return; Financial Performance; Corporate Social Responsibility; Price To Earnings Ratio; Indonesian Banks

title: Jornada Científica Estudiantil 2026
summary: La Jornada Científica Estudiantil UF 2026, desarrollada bajo el lema “Investigación, Innovación y Transformación Social: Construyendo Soluciones para el Futuro”, permitió la generación de un espacio académico destinado al encuentro, reflexión y socialización de experiencias investigativas surgidas desde la formación superior tecnológica. En ella, estudiantes y docentes compartieron propuestas orientadas al análisis de problemáticas contemporáneas, reconocimiento de oportunidades de innovación y búsqueda de respuestas aplicables a los desafíos que enfrentan las organizaciones, emprendimientos y la sociedad. La presente publicación nace con el propósito de conservar y proyectar ese ejercicio académico. Más que reunir una sucesión de exposiciones, busca recuperar el pensamiento, inquietudes, hallazgos y propuestas que dieron sentido a cada ponencia. Cada contribución, representa un proceso particular de aproximación al conocimiento y expresa la manera en que sus autores observaron una realidad, formularon preguntas, analizaron información y construyeron alternativas desde su área de formación.Los trabajos presentados evidencian la amplitud temática que caracterizó a la jornada. La innovación empresarial, el emprendimiento y la transformación digital estuvieron presentes en investigaciones relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial, posicionamiento de emprendimientos, incorporación de tecnologías a pequeños negocios y la creación de propuestas educativas inclusivas. Al mismo tiempo, la gestión empresarial y del talento humano fue abordada desde perspectivas vinculadas con la capacitación, motivación, el clima laboral, resolución de conflictos y la necesidad de fortalecer las estructuras internas de las pequeñas empresas.El comercio exterior ocupó, igualmente, un espacio relevante dentro de la jornada. Las investigaciones analizaron procesos de modernización aduanera, logística inversa, automatización, sostenibilidad, criterios ESG, acuerdos comerciales y aplicación de inteligencia artificial en las cadenas de suministro. Estas aproximaciones permitieron reconocer que la transformación tecnológica modifica no sólo los procedimientos y herramientas utilizados por las organizaciones, sino también las competencias profesionales, formas de tomar decisiones y las condiciones necesarias para participar en entornos económicos cada vez más interconectados. Una característica especialmente valiosa de los trabajos reunidos es su cercanía con problemas concretos. Las ponencias no se limitaron a describir conceptos; abordaron interrogantes relacionadas con la realidad de pequeños negocios, trabajadores, emprendedores, empresas exportadoras e importadoras, operadores logísticos y jóvenes que requieren nuevas oportunidades de formación. Esta orientación permitió articular la investigación académica con situaciones susceptibles de análisis, intervención y mejora. La Jornada Científica Estudiantil representó, también, una oportunidad formativa. Investigar implica aprender a formular preguntas, seleccionar información, construir métodos de análisis, interpretar resultados y comunicar ideas con claridad. Presentar esos resultados ante una comunidad académica añade una dimensión fundamental: permite someter las propuestas al diálogo, fortalecer la argumentación y reconocer que el conocimiento se construye colectivamente. En este sentido, la presente memoria no debe entenderse únicamente como un registro de lo acontecido. Constituye también una evidencia del proceso de formación investigativa, una expresión del compromiso de estudiantes y docentes con la producción de conocimiento y un punto de partida para futuras investigaciones. Las preguntas planteadas, los resultados obtenidos y las propuestas formuladas pueden abrir nuevas líneas de estudio, ser profundizadas posteriormente o convertirse en referencias para la formulación de proyectos académicos y profesionales. La innovación, transversal en muchas de estas contribuciones, no se reduce a la incorporación de tecnología. También se expresa en la capacidad de observar los problemas desde nuevas perspectivas, adaptar metodologías, fortalecer procesos, proponer modelos de gestión y crear condiciones para que los cambios tecnológicos puedan integrarse de manera responsable a las organizaciones y a la sociedad. Esta visión se encuentra particularmente representada en trabajos que vinculan tecnología e inclusión y que sostienen que innovar implica, además, construir condiciones para que las oportunidades de la transformación digital puedan alcanzar a un mayor número de personas. En correspondencia, la Memoria de reportes de la Jornada Científica Estudiantil UF 2026 se presenta, por tanto, como un testimonio del esfuerzo intelectual y formativo desarrollado durante este encuentro. En sus páginas convergen preguntas, datos, aprendizajes, propuestas y reflexiones que muestran a la investigación como una herramienta para comprender el presente y participar activamente en la construcción del futuro.Conservar estos aportes significa reconocer el valor de cada experiencia investigativa y, al mismo tiempo, mantener abierta la conversación que comenzó durante la jornada. Cada ponencia constituye una invitación a continuar preguntando, analizando, innovando y construyendo soluciones desde el conocimiento, la responsabilidad académica y el compromiso con la transformación social.
