title: Barriers to Blockchain Adoption in Circular Supply Chain Management: A Systematic Review and TISM-MICMAC Analysis
summary: This study examines the practical challenges organizations encounter in adopting blockchain for circular supply chain management.The objective is to provide actionable insights for managers and policymakers to facilitate blockchain adoption for strengthening circularity within supply chains and enhancing circular supply chain performance.A comprehensive systematic literature review is conducted with 34 articles to identify key barriers.Subsequently, the key barriers were modeled using inputs from nine experts through Total Interpretive Structural Modelling (TISM) and MICMAC analysis.The results indicate that barriers such as lack of government regulations and lack of stakeholder involvement function as root-level drivers, while mid-level feedback barriers include cost, lack of trust, and lack of standardization.At the upper level, outcome barriers such as security, privacy, and scalability emerge as dependent effects.The findings highlight that successful blockchain adoption in circular supply chains requires first strengthening institutional and collaborative foundations, followed by addressing technical limitations.Overall, the study emphasizes realworld implementation considerations and the adoption of circular economy principles within blockchain-enabled supply chain transformation.

title: pdf Conceptual Model of Public Sector Financial Reporting Based on Siri’ na Pesse
summary: Research Objectives - This study aims to develop a conceptual framework for public sector financial reporting based on the local wisdom values of Siri’ na Pesse to strengthen information integrity, accountability, transparency, and an orientation toward community welfare. Method - This study employs a qualitative approach using a literature review and document analysis. The data are analyzed through thematic analysis and conceptual synthesis of relevant academic literature, previous studies, regulations, and public sector accounting standards. Research Findings - The findings indicate that the values of Siri’ na Pesse have the potential to serve as an ethical foundation for public sector financial reporting, rather than as a substitute for applicable accounting standards. The five conceptual elements of Siri’ na Pesse-based budgeting—inner moral sensitivity, local wisdom values, budget performance, welfare, and human dignity—can be interpreted in terms of their relevance to government financial accountability. This synthesis produces a conceptual model that connects local values with information integrity, accountability and transparency, as well as the relationship between financial information, performance, and public benefits. Theory and Practical Implications - Theoretically, this study extends the discussion of Siri’ na Pesse from the contexts of budgeting and community participation to the perspective of public sector financial reporting. Practically, this framework may serve as a reference for local governments seeking to strengthen reporting ethics, information disclosure, and accountability for the use of public resources while remaining compliant with Government Accounting Standards. Novelty - The novelty of this study lies in the development of a conceptual framework that positions Siri’ na Pesse as an ethical foundation for integrating local wisdom with the principles of public sector financial reporting.

title: ADOPTION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: BARRIERS AND ENABLERS IN DEVELOPING ECONOMIES
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology capable of enhancing efficiency, decision-making, and resilience in supply chain management. However, its adoption in developing economies remains constrained by several technological, organizational, and environmental challenges. This study examined the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management, with emphasis on the barriers and enablers in developing economies, using Nigeria as the study context. A cross-sectional survey research design was adopted, and data were collected from 235 employees, managers, and supply chain professionals in selected manufacturing firms, logistics companies, retail organizations, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria using a structured questionnaire titled Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Supply Chain Management Index (AIASCMI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson Product Moment Correlation. The findings revealed that identified barriers, including inadequate digital infrastructure, high implementation costs, shortage of skilled personnel, and organizational challenges, have a significant negative relationship with the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. The study also found that identified enablers, such as top management support, technological readiness, employee competence, and government support, significantly influence the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence. The study concludes that overcoming existing barriers while strengthening organizational and technological capabilities is essential for the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. It is recommended that organizations invest in digital infrastructure, workforce development, and supportive management practices to maximize the benefits of Artificial Intelligence and improve supply chain performance.

title: ADOPTION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT: BARRIERS AND ENABLERS IN DEVELOPING ECONOMIES
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology capable of enhancing efficiency, decision-making, and resilience in supply chain management. However, its adoption in developing economies remains constrained by several technological, organizational, and environmental challenges. This study examined the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management, with emphasis on the barriers and enablers in developing economies, using Nigeria as the study context. A cross-sectional survey research design was adopted, and data were collected from 235 employees, managers, and supply chain professionals in selected manufacturing firms, logistics companies, retail organizations, and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria using a structured questionnaire titled Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Supply Chain Management Index (AIASCMI). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson Product Moment Correlation. The findings revealed that identified barriers, including inadequate digital infrastructure, high implementation costs, shortage of skilled personnel, and organizational challenges, have a significant negative relationship with the adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. The study also found that identified enablers, such as top management support, technological readiness, employee competence, and government support, significantly influence the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence. The study concludes that overcoming existing barriers while strengthening organizational and technological capabilities is essential for the successful adoption of Artificial Intelligence in supply chain management. It is recommended that organizations invest in digital infrastructure, workforce development, and supportive management practices to maximize the benefits of Artificial Intelligence and improve supply chain performance.

title: Human-Resource Digital Transformation Trends in Private Universities in India
summary: The digital transformation is reshaping the functioning of academic, administrative and human-resource operations in higher education institutions. The study focuses on the implementation of digital HR in the private Universities of India, specifically on the following digital HR practices: payroll automation, employee self-service, online recruitment, digital performance appraisal, learning management systems, artificial intelligence (AI), and HR analytics. The descriptive survey design was adopted and the data were obtained from 60 HR professionals and administrative personnel in private higher education institutions. The results indicate that high adoption of payroll automation and employee self-service portals and on the other hand, AI-based recruitment and HR analytics are still in their early stages. Financial challenges, employee resistance, lack of digital skills, integration of systems and data-security issues are the main challenges identified. The results have shown that the HR automation process in private Universities is moving from simple automation to more sophisticated and data-oriented HR processes; however, sophisticated digital HR is still at its beginning stage.

title: Pengaruh Penghindaran Pajak, Kepemilikan Manajerial, dan Komite Audit terhadap Nilai Perusahaan
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of tax avoidance, managerial ownership, and the audit committee on firm value for industrial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2020–2024 period. The analytical method employed is multiple linear regression, incorporating both simultaneous and partial tests. The results indicate that, simultaneously, tax avoidance, managerial ownership, and the audit committee have a significant influence on firm value. This suggests that these three variables, when considered collectively, are relevant determinants in shaping investor perception of a company's value. However, the partial test results reveal that only managerial ownership has a significant effect on firm value, demonstrating that the alignment of interests between managers and shareholders through equity ownership is a mechanism positively responded to by the market. Conversely, tax avoidance and the audit committee, when examined individually, do not exert a significant influence on firm value within the industrial sector during the observed period. These findings provide insights for corporate management regarding the importance of ownership structure as a signal to investors, as well as the need to evaluate the effectiveness of other corporate governance policies in optimizing firm value.

title: Accounting Logic Sequencing in SAP ECC: A Graph-to-Event-Log Transformation for Audit-Ready Process Mining
summary: This paper addresses a core challenge in accounting information systems: reconstructing audit-compliant business process sequences from ERP accounting data that is structurally graph-based rather than sequentially ordered. Traditional timestamp-driven process mining fails to capture the logical order imposed by open item accounting, resulting in misleading process models for auditors. We propose a novel preprocessing algorithm that transforms financial process mining (FPM) instance graphs extracted from SAP ECC 6.0 accounting tables (BKPF/BSEG) into sequential event logs that respect accounting logic. Using a real-world dataset from a news agency's 2011 fiscal year, we demonstrate that our method reduces process model complexity by 53% and improves alignment with expected accounting workflows such as goods receipt → invoice → payment. This research enables auditors to leverage process mining directly on accounting data, bridging the gap between ERP financial records and actionable audit intelligence.

title: The Relationship Between Financial Managers’ Leadership Style and the Quality of Financial Reporting in Organizations
summary: This study was conducted to examine the relationship between financial managers’ leadership style and the quality of financial reporting in organizations. This research is applied in terms of purpose and descriptive-correlational in terms of implementation method. The statistical population consisted of all financial managers, accountants, and auditors employed in organizations. A sample of 212 participants was selected using stratified random sampling. Data were collected using the standardized Multifactor Leadership Questionnaire (MLQ) and the Financial Reporting Quality Questionnaire developed by Kawasi (2021). Data analysis was performed at both descriptive and inferential levels using Structural Equation Modeling based on the Partial Least Squares approach (PLS-SEM) through SmartPLS version 3 software. The results indicated a positive and strong relationship between transformational leadership style and financial reporting quality (β = 0.552, t-value = 8.899), a positive and moderate relationship between transactional leadership style and financial reporting quality (β = 0.358, t-value = 3.429), and a negative and weak relationship between laissez-faire leadership style and financial reporting quality (β = -0.259, t-value = 2.675). All relationships were statistically significant at the 95% confidence level. Financial managers who adopt a transformational leadership style, characterized by inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, and individualized consideration, can significantly enhance the quality of financial reporting. In contrast, the laissez-faire leadership style exerts an adverse effect on reporting quality. Therefore, emphasizing transformational leadership competencies in the selection and development of financial managers is recommended as a key behavioral factor for improving the transparency and reliability of financial information.

title: Breaking Data Silos in Demand Planning in Humanitarian Medical Supply Chains using AI
summary: Humanitarian medical supply chains operate under extreme uncertainty, long lead times and fragmented data. Over 300 million people in 72 countries need humanitarian assistance, and supply chains are central to delivering life-saving supplies (Nieto, Jaschke & Piperno, 2025). This poster examines how data silos constrain demand planning, using Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) as a case study. Interviews with field demand-planning professionals were used to map the data needed for needs forecasting and to rate each source for reliability and criticality to planning. Barriers and enablers to AI adoption were then analysed across financial, technical, ethical and cultural/organisational dimensions. The findings show that data fragmentation is a structural constraint on decision performance. Planning relies on manual consolidation and spreadsheets, planning cycles run 6–8 months, and the expert forecaster becomes the bottleneck. The poster proposes an AI-enabled data flow in which an agent harmonises country-level variation in Ministry of Health standard definitions before data are integrated. A hybrid integration layer then supports forecasting, scenario analysis and supply decisions, with humans kept in the loop. The aim is to improve organisational sense-making, not to automate decisions. The poster also outlines an implementation roadmap and future directions: digital twinning, external risk signals and wider multi-agency use.
